funding_notes: Domain this.co matches (THIS™ plant-based meat, London). Seed £8.7m date not stated in sources (pre-June 2021). Series B £15m includes £4.7m Seedrs equity crowdfunding; Series C £20m mixes primary and secondary (split undisclosed), so amount_raised overstates new capital. A separate 2020 crowd raise of >£4m excluded from rounds (imprecise amount). Kreos Capital listed as backer is likely debt; excluded. Company said £35m raised 2019–mid-2024 before Series C.

name: Veratrak
description: Smarter analytics, collaboration tools and record-keeping for pharmaceutical supply chain companies
funding_notes: Domain veratrak.com matches. Seedtable lists this as a $6M 'Series A' (tracker); company calls it Seed. Earlier pre-seed (Seedcamp) amounts not captured.

name: Fluidstack
description: AI cloud platform that aggregates underutilised GPUs from global data centres to deliver high‑performance, scalable GPU compute for AI/ML
funding_notes: Domain fluidstack.io matches (also fluidstack.com). Series A ($7.5B valuation) closed Jan 2026, disclosed 2026-07-20. Excluded: reported ~$1.5B Jane Street-led round at $18B (Forbes, Sept 2026) — not confirmed by company, treated as unconfirmed; tracker-only $3M 2019 seed and $200M Feb 2025 'Series A' (Seedtable/Sacra), 2024 $24.7M SAFE, and debt facilities.

name: Doctorly
description: Manage your medical practice with one simple system
funding_notes: Domain doctorly.de matches (Berlin). Filed for insolvency March 2025; fully acquired by FREY ADV (FREY group) June 2025, insolvency application withdrawn. Series A total $17.2M per company.

name: Sweatcoin
description: Digital currency backed by physical movement
funding_notes: Domain sweatco.in matches (SweatCo Ltd / Sweat Economy). Excluded: July 2022 $13M Sweat Economy raise 'including a private token sale' (equity/token split undisclosed; The Block called it a round led by Spartan Capital) — token sales excluded per rules.

name: Pace
description: Intelligent pricing for the hospitality industry. Using machine learning to find the right price
funding_notes: Input description is wrong: paceup.com was Pace Revenue, a London hotel dynamic-pricing/revenue-management SaaS (not restaurant CRM). paceup.com now returns 404. Acquired by FLYR Labs (FLYR Hospitality) Sept 2022, terms undisclosed. Tracker-only later seed rounds (2019 Impact X, 2021 Cur8 per Dealroom) excluded.

name: StepLadder
description: Collaborative financing enabling you to get your home deposit 45% faster on average
funding_notes: Domain joinstepladder.com matches. UKTN (Mar 2021) says £3m raised in total and a Seedrs equity crowdfunding campaign was opened; crowdfunding result not captured.

name: PassFort
description: Automated AML & KYC onboarding
funding_notes: Acquisition confirmed: acquired by Moody's (Moody's Analytics KYC) Dec 2021, undisclosed price; passfort.com is legacy domain. Headline $16.2M Sept 2021 raise = $11.3M Series A equity + ~$4.9M venture debt from Shard Credit Partners (debt excluded). Tracker-only 2015/2017 seed rounds (£610k, £730k per Dealroom) excluded.

name: SeedLegals
description: Raise. Invest. Legals. Sorted.
funding_notes: Domain seedlegals.com matches. No later priced round found in public press; earlier seed amounts not captured.

name: Flow
description: Revolutionising hardware development, starting with the most collaborative requirements management tool in the world
funding_notes: Identity verified: flowengineering.com is Flow Engineering, a requirements-management/systems-engineering platform for hardware teams (founder Pari Singh; London, HQ moved to San Francisco) — not HVAC optimization; input description is wrong. Series A date from Fortune exclusive (company blog post dated Nov 2025).

name: 9fin
description: AI powered financial data platform for fixed income
funding_notes: Domain 9fin.com matches. amount_raised blank: mixed GBP/USD rounds; company states >$250M raised to date after the $170M Series C ($1.3B valuation). 2019 ~$2.5M seed led by Fly Ventures is tracker-only (Cointime), excluded.

name: Nevercode
description: Cloud-based continuous integration & delivery for iOS, Android, Cordova, Ionic, React Native & Flutter projects
funding_notes: Nevercode Ltd (Estonia/London, founders Triin Kask and Kristian Sägi) operates Codemagic; codemagic.io is its current domain (legacy nevercode.io). Company blog (Jan 2019) confirms a $1.5M investment from Venrex but gives no stage; only trackers (Dealroom/Tracxn/CB Insights) call it seed, so round type unclear. Date approximate ('recently' as of late 2018/Jan 2019).

name: Bloomsbury
description: Enabling everyone to rapidly create text understanding applications
funding_notes: Bloomsbury AI (London NLP, Cape Q&A API; Entrepreneur First alum, UCL spinout). Acquired by Facebook July 2018 (reported $23–30M, cash+stock). bloomsbury.ai now shows only a farewell page ('Thank you for sharing the ride with us'). Summer-2017 seed amount undisclosed; total ~ $1.7M reported by SiliconANGLE (includes ~$13.6k EF pre-seed), so amount_raised left blank.

name: Zamna
description: Strategic data sharing for airlines, enabled through blockchain.
funding_notes: Zamna (zamna.com), London-based passenger identity/data verification platform for airlines and border agencies; formerly VChain Technology (renamed 2019). Not iRespond/Blockpass lineage. Seedcamp pre-seed Jan 2017 (as Vchain); IAG Hangar 51 accelerator investment Apr 2017 (undisclosed); $5M seed Oct 2019 led by LocalGlobe and Oxford Capital. Dec 2022 Travolution: raising a pre-Series A ahead of a planned Series A, with ex-Amadeus president Julia Sattel investing; no amount or close found.

name: Labstep
description: Capturing real-time scientific process data to improve research and enable collaboration.
funding_notes: Labstep (labstep.com), London/Oxford electronic lab notebook (ELN) platform. Seedcamp-backed (date and amount of its initial investment not disclosed). Company release says £1M raised from angel investors in June 2018 (TechCrunch: including existing investors). Acquired by STARLIMS Aug 22, 2023. A 2017 £500k Seedcamp tranche and a 2021 ~$710k round appear only on trackers, so they are left out.

name: Wevat
description: Digitising tax free shopping by allowing non-EU travellers to confirm their eligibility, record purchases and claim back Value Added Tax.
funding_notes: Wevat (wevat.com) is a digital VAT/tax-free shopping refund app (London-founded, now focused on UK travellers shopping in France), NOT EV charging payments; the input description is wrong. Seedcamp pre-seed Jan 2017. Company team page says the founders 'have raised £3.5m' in total, with no round breakdown. A 2019 Series A (Firstminute, JamJar, Salica, Sweet Capital, Andy Phillips) and a 2020 convertible note (Entrée Capital) appear only on trackers, with no primary press found.

name: CyberSmart
description: Automated compliance to protect your organisation and data

funding_rounds.stage: Series A extension (amount undisclosed; total raised >$10M)

funding_notes: CyberSmart (cybersmart.co.uk), London SME cybersecurity, Cyber Essentials certification and bundled cyber insurance; came out of the GCHQ/NCSC Cyber Accelerator in 2017. IQ Capital backed it from the seed round (seed amount not public). TechCrunch says ~£8M raised before the Series B. A March 2025 £3.52M round led by Cambridge Angels is tracker-only. Founderpath revenue financing ($1.4M) is debt and is left out.

name: Cuvva
description: Pay-as-you-drive insurance on your terms.
last_round_type: Equity round incl. Seedrs crowdfunding (EIS; round type not labelled)

funding_rounds.stage: Equity round incl. Seedrs crowdfunding (EIS; round type not labelled)

funding_notes: Cuvva (cuvva.com), London app-based flexible/hourly and subscription car insurance. The Jan 2017 seed brought its total to £2M, so about £0.5M of earlier funding has no published detail. The 2022 Seedrs campaign was at a £108.5M pre-money; its £4.03M total includes £2.05M from existing and institutional investors. £6.37M of outstanding convertible notes converted in that round; they are left out as debt.

name: Telleroo
description: Bulk payments simplified
funding_notes: Telleroo (telleroo.com), London FCA-authorised bulk supplier/payroll payments platform that integrates with Xero and QuickBooks (CEO Fabian Flatz). Seedcamp pre-seed announced Jan 2017; Speedinvest lists it as a portfolio company. Small seed rounds (~$120k Nov 2016, £95k Dec 2016, $513k May 2017) and a 2022 round appear only on trackers, with no primary press found.

name: Fraugster
description: Using AI to eliminate e-commerce fraud and increase customers’ profits.

funding_rounds.stage: Venture round (type not stated; precedes Series B)

funding_notes: Fraugster (fraugster.com), Berlin/Tel Aviv AI payment-fraud detection. Tech.eu reported the Jan 2017 round as €4.7M. Seedcamp invested in late 2016 (amount undisclosed). Trackers also list a €3.6M Series A in 2016, but no primary press was found for it. Provisional insolvency began Jan 2023 and the business closed around end of March 2023 (DistressWire).

name: Legit Patents
description: AI-powered Intellectual Property Department

investors: founding members of Uber Advanced Technologies Center

notable_investors: founding members of Uber Advanced Technologies Center
funding_notes: Legit / Legit Patents (legit.ai), Cambridge MA AI/NLP platform that helps inventors draft patents (CEO Matt Osman). legit.ai returned a server error when fetched, so it may be inactive. Seedcamp seed Nov 2016 (amount undisclosed). Also received a Y Combinator Fellowship and an EU Seal of Excellence in 2016; neither is counted as a round.

name: viz.ai
description: Viz.ai alerts multidisciplinary care teams earlier in the workflow, to coordinate care and connect frontline health care professionals (HCPs) to specialists and facilitate efficient communication and care coordination.
funding_notes: viz.ai verified. San Francisco AI care-coordination/stroke-detection platform (CEO Chris Mansi). Series A $21M (Kleiner Perkins, July 2018), Series B $50M (Greenoaks, Oct 2019), Series C $71M (Scale + Insight, Mar 2021), Series D $100M (Tiger Global + Insight, Apr 7, 2022, $1.2B valuation). amount_raised is the sum of these four sourced equity rounds; an earlier seed and a reported ~$40M 2023 debt facility (tracker-only) are excluded.

name: Libryo
description: SaaS for regulatory law. Providing certainty to compliance professionals, by answering their legal questions at their time and place.
funding_notes: Libryo (libryo.com), London/Cape Town EHS regulatory compliance intelligence platform. Seed first closed at £787k and reached £950k at a second close (company blog). Seedcamp had made an earlier initial investment (amount undisclosed). The May 2021 £1.35M round, led by Future Energy Ventures with the UK Future Fund and Nextlaw Ventures, was a convertible note, so it is left out as debt. EU Horizon 2020 Seal of Excellence was a certificate, not a grant. Acquired by ERM Dec 2022 (terms undisclosed).

name: CRU Kafe
description: The finest Organic coffee from around the world, in the convenience of a Nespresso® friendly capsule
funding_notes: CRU Kafe (crukafe.com), London organic/Fairtrade Nespresso-compatible coffee pods and a B Corp. It sells pods, not ready-to-drink coffee as the input says. Seedcamp led the £1.25M seed in Oct 2016. Earlier: Kickstarter, plus about £800k raised by Nov 2015 (unitemised), and a Nov 2015 Seedrs equity campaign targeting £300k whose close was not confirmed, so it is left out. A £900k Oct 2025 round appears only on trackers.

name: Wave
description: The platform for creating and sharing virtual concerts
funding_notes: Wave (wavexr.com; formerly TheWaveVR), an XR/virtual concert platform (Austin, later LA; CEO Adam Arrigo). This is not Wave the mobile money company (wave.com). wavexr.com returned a server error when fetched. Funding total was $40M after the Series B (GeekWire). No Seedcamp-specific round was found in public press.

name: Reposit
description: The tenancy deposit alternative.
funding_notes: Reposit (reposit.co.uk, live), London FCA-authorised tenancy deposit alternative. The 2016 seed was reported as £400k ($520k). The 2018 £500k round brought total raised to £950k, which implies about £50k more than the itemised rounds. Rounds in Jan 2019 (~$700k) and Apr 2020 (~£800k) appear only on trackers. Graduated from the Ignite accelerator.

name: Vinterior
description: A two-sided marketplace connecting professional furniture sellers to buyers of vintage and design furniture.
funding_notes: Vinterior (vinterior.co), London curated vintage/pre-owned furniture marketplace (CEO Sandrine Zhang Ferron). Joined Seedcamp's pre-seed cohort June 2016. Channel 4 says total raised reached £15M after its £3M media-for-equity deal; Insider Media says £12M including that deal. The crowdfunding raised 'more than £1M', recorded here as £1M. Venrex-backed seed rounds in 2017-2020 have no public amounts beyond trackers.

name: KareInn
description: Improving the quality of life for our parents’ generation.
funding_notes: KareInn (kareinn.com), London digital care-planning software for care homes (co-founders Eric Kihlstrom, Alexander Kenney and John Lanyon). Joined Seedcamp's pre-seed cohort June 2016. A Start Up Loans case study says founders took £30k in director Start Up Loans (debt, left out) and later brought on angel investors (amounts undisclosed). Acquired by Person Centred Software in mid-2024. A ~$251k seed in June 2016 appears only on trackers.

name: Trail
description: Smart daily checklist for operations management.
funding_notes: Trail (trailapp.com), London hospitality digital checklist and operations/compliance app (co-founders Joe Cripps and Wil Grace). £900k 'late seed' in Aug 2016. Acquired by The Access Group (Access Hospitality) on Aug 4, 2021. No other rounds found in primary press.

name: Thriva
description: Thriva offers a personalized at-home finger-prick blood test which enables individuals to easily track and improve health.
funding_notes: Thriva (thriva.co), London at-home finger-prick blood testing / proactive health company founded 2016 by Hamish Grierson, Eliot Brooks and Tom Livesey. £1.5M seed (Jun 2017, incl. Seedcamp, 500 Startups, LCIF), £6M Series A (Jul 2019), £4M Series A extension led by Target Global (May 2020); company stated total £11M (sum of announced rounds £11.5M). A filings-derived tracker (Sonde, Companies House SH01s) shows a ~£150k May 2016 allotment (likely the early Seedcamp/pre-seed) and a £5.7M allotment in Jan 2021 that likely corresponds to the extension close; no later public equity round found.

name: Alterest
description: Institutional-grade data and tools for private and alternative credit
funding_notes: Alterest (alterest.co), London platform/data for private and alternative credit and marketplace-lending deal lifecycle (joined Seedcamp Jan 2016 as 'Alterest Investment'). Company blog announced in Nov 2019 an investment round led by angel Sean Tai (founder of Debtdomain), amount and stage not disclosed. Amounts ($83K 2016, $652K 2019) appear only on trackers (Tracxn/PitchBook-type), not primary press; SFC Capital also listed as investor by a tracker. No public priced seed found.

name: Juro
description: The contract collaboration platform: contract management software your whole team will love
funding_notes: Juro (juro.com), London contract automation/collaboration platform founded 2016 by Richard Mabey and Pavel Kovalevich. $750K Jan 2017 round (CEO says really an angel round), $2M seed led by Point Nine (Apr 2018), Series A announced as $5M, precise $5.25M per Business Wire/WSGR (Jan 2020, USV lead), $23.25M Series B led by Eight Roads (Jan 2022). Company states $31.5M total; sum of announced rounds is $31.25M.

name: Beeline
description: A revolutionary navigation system to transform your ride in the city

grants.name: European Space Agency
Innovate UK

funding_notes: Beeline (beeline.co; Relish Technologies Ltd), London two-wheel navigation devices/app for cyclists and motorcyclists (Velo, Moto) founded 2015 by Mark Jenner and Tom Putnam; not Beeline.com staffing software. Seedcamp-backed Jan 2016; £500k first seed round (Sep 2016) incl. Seedcamp, EarlyMarket, LCIF, TrueStart and Seedrs; £1.01M Seedrs equity crowdfund at £8M pre-money (Sep 2022). ESA and Innovate UK grants mentioned without amounts; the 2024 Moto II Kickstarter (~£654k) is product pre-sales, not equity, and is excluded.

name: Cronofy
description: APIs for calendar connectivity and interview scheduling automation

funding_rounds.stage: Growth investment (unlabelled; partial secondary exit for seed investors)

funding_notes: Cronofy (cronofy.com), Nottingham/London calendar-sync and scheduling API company founded by Adam Bird and Garry Shutler; Seedcamp investment Dec 2014. $1.6M seed led by Firestartr (Jan 2016); £15M BGF investment (May 2025), not labelled as a series and partly a secondary exit for seed investors (some trackers call it Series A). Mixed USD/GBP, and the BGF primary/secondary split is undisclosed, so amount_raised left blank.

name: Kasko
description: Digital end-to-end platform for bespoke on-demand insurance.
funding_notes: KASKO (kasko.io), London insurtech-as-a-service platform for launching digital/on-demand insurance products, founded 2015 by Nikolaus Sühr and Matthew Wardle; Seedcamp-backed. Only trackers (Dealroom) report £450k (Oct 2015) and £830k (Dec 2017) rounds via the Angels Den angel platform, plus a small grant and an undisclosed 2022 'Series A' listing; no primary press announcement found, and a 2021 interview said the company was largely bootstrapped and preparing a Series A.

name: Charlie HR
description: The free HR platform for small businesses.
funding_notes: CharlieHR (charliehr.com), London HR software for small businesses founded by Rob O'Donovan and Ben Gateley. £1M seed led by Connect Ventures with Seedcamp (Mar 2016); ADV invested in May 2017 (amount undisclosed). A ~$1.8M May 2020 round with 500 Startups appears only on aggregators (Nordic9/Tracxn) and is excluded from the total.

name: Wefox
description: wefox is a category-defining insurtech platform that is connecting insurance companies, distributors, and customers, to give the world simple access to digital insurance solutions.
funding_notes: wefox (wefox.com), Berlin/Zurich insurtech (originally FinanceFox, which joined Seedcamp Jan 2016) founded by Julian Teicke, Fabian Wesemann and Dario Fazlic. $5.5M seed (Jan 2016) and $28M Series A (Sep 2016; wefox later cites $30M/2017) as FinanceFox; $235M Series B (2019); $650M Series C at $3B (2021; company says $918M raised to that point); $400M Series D at $4.5B (2022, TechCrunch says equity plus debt); $55M equity second close plus a $55M JPM/Barclays credit facility, which is excluded (2023); €25M investor capital during the 2024 restructuring. amount_raised left blank because the Series D equity/debt split is undisclosed and currencies are mixed.

name: AI Build
description: Developing Artificial Intelligence and 3D printing technologies to make manufacturing easier and smarter

funding_rounds.stage: Funding round (unlabelled; trackers call it seed)

funding_notes: Ai Build / Aibuild (ai-build.com), London AI software (AiSync) for automating large-scale industrial 3D printing/additive manufacturing, founded 2015 by architects Daghan Cam and Michail Desyllas; Seedcamp is an existing investor. £730k seed led by SuperSeed (Feb 2021), $3.2M round led by ACT Venture Partners (Jun 2022), $8.5M (~£7M) Series A led by IQ Capital with Nikon (Oct 2023). amount_raised left blank because the rounds mix GBP and USD.

name: Much Better Adventures
description: Global marketplace for holidays and experiences from specialist local hosts.
funding_notes: Much Better Adventures (muchbetteradventures.com), London adventure-travel marketplace with local hosts, founded 2012 by Alex Narracott, Sam Bruce and Guy Bowden; joined Seedcamp in 2015. £400k seed with Seedcamp and LCIF (Feb 2016); equity crowdfunds of £1.25M (Crowdcube, closed Jan 2018), >£1.2M (Seedrs, 2019) and 'just over £1M' at public launch (Seedrs, 2021; final amount not confirmed in primary sources, so excluded from total); £5M from Gresham House Ventures (Dec 2024). amount_raised £7.85M excludes the 2021 round.

name: SwiftShift
description: SwiftShift is reimagining pediatric home care delivery by creating the first caregiver-managed pediatric home care service.
funding_notes: SwiftShift (swiftshift.com), founded 2012 by Assaf Shalvi (with Dan Sandhu) as a London/Israel real-time shift-filling workforce tool, now a US caregiver-managed pediatric home care service. Domain and founder match, so this is the same company after a pivot; the pediatric description is confirmed. Primary press covers only an undisclosed 2014 Indian Angel Network investment and a Seedcamp investment (Jan 2016). Rounds of £600k seed (2014, Episode 1/Ankur/IAN/UpWest), $2.7M seed (2016, Freestyle/Crosslink/Bowery), $2M (2017) and a $5.7M Series A (2018) appear only on trackers (StartupRanking/Dealroom), so they are excluded.

name: TalkPush
description: Building solutions to facilitate conversations with large talent pools via chat, messaging, and voice.
funding_notes: Talkpush (talkpush.com), Hong Kong-founded (2014, Max Armbruster) recruitment automation and conversational hiring platform with operations in the Philippines and LatAm. The company's own timeline says it completed a seed round in Nov 2015 with 500 Startups, Seedcamp and angels (amount undisclosed). Latin Leap invested in Apr 2020 (undisclosed; some trackers label it Series A). Caveat: seed+ rests on the company's own 'Seed Round' label with accelerator-type investors and no disclosed amount, so it could be downgraded to unclear.

name: Pleo
description: The company credit card reimagined.
funding_notes: Pleo (pleo.io), Copenhagen spend-management / smart company card fintech founded 2015 by Jeppe Rindom and Niccolo Perra (ex-Tradeshift). $5.5M seed in two parts ($3M Founders-led 2016, $3.25M Creandum-led with Seedcamp 2017), $16M Series A (2018), $56M Series B (2019), $150M Series C at $1.7B (Jul 2021) and a $200M extension at $4.7B (Dec 2021, Series C total $350M). A €40M HSBC Innovation Banking debt facility (2024) is excluded; no later equity round found.

name: WealthKernel
description: Automated wealth management as a service to institutional clients.
funding_notes: WealthKernel (wealthkernel.com), London API-based digital investment/wealth infrastructure (B2B robo/embedded investing) founded 2015 by Karan Shanmugarajah. £4.5M Series A led by ETFS Capital (Jan 2020), $7M Series A+ led by XTX Ventures (Jan 2022) and £6M Series A extension led by ETFS (Jan 2024); ETFS says it first invested in 2018. A ~$1M 2017 seed led by Seedcamp with LCIF appears only on aggregators and is excluded; amount_raised left blank because of mixed GBP/USD.

name: Getagent
description: Find the best estate agent to sell your home, in just a few clicks.
funding_notes: GetAgent (getagent.co.uk; Getagent Ltd, Companies House 09428979), London data-driven estate agent comparison site co-founded by Colby Short. Seedcamp Seed Fund investment in 2015; £2.2M super-seed led by Marchmont Ventures with the Channel 4 Commercial Growth Fund (Mar 2019). A filings-derived tracker (Sonde) shows further allotments (about £2.1M 2016, £2.2M 2018, £2.5M Feb 2019, £1.5M May 2023; ~£8.4M total), but no primary press, so those are excluded.

name: Priori Data
description: Quantify the app economy.
funding_notes: Priori Data (prioridata.com; Priori Data GmbH), Berlin app-store intelligence/analytics company founded by ex-Morgan Stanley analyst Patrick Kane. $1M seed from unnamed angels and private individuals (May 2014); Seedcamp Seed Fund portfolio by Sep 2015 (amount undisclosed). Acquired by AIM-listed appScatter in Jul 2018 for £13.5M (£1.8M cash + £11.7M shares). Caveat: the only priced 'seed' was angel-funded.

name: JOBDOH
description: A quick location based booking platform to get quality temporary workers for hospitality and exhibitions
funding_notes: JOBDOH (jobdoh.com), Hong Kong on-demand temp-staffing marketplace for hospitality/exhibitions (founder/CEO Xania Wong). Seedcamp invested after Seedcamp Week London (announced Feb 2015); also backed by Swire's Blueprint accelerator and Loyal VC (accelerator-style, 2019; Loyal now lists it as Inactive). No priced seed round or amounts published by primary sources; databases only show tiny/undisclosed amounts.

name: Pollen
description: Pay and collect funds around the world quickly, cheaply and efficiently.
funding_notes: Pollen Technologies (pollentechnologies.com), London FCA-authorised (FRN 768011) white-label payments/banking platform, founded 2015 — not Pollen.co or Pollen VC. Described as backed by Seedcamp, Level39 and Q-Advisers, but no primary press release discloses rounds. Tracxn alone lists a $113K 'Seed' (Nov 2015) and a $500K 'Series A' (Oct 2023); unverified, so round type/amounts left blank.

name: Edgefolio
description: The platform connecting Investors and Fund Managers through data.
funding_notes: Edgefolio (edgefolio.com), London/Norway-origin fund-distribution and cap-intro platform for hedge funds. Seedcamp investment announced Feb 2015 (undisclosed). CEO Rowen Pillay told DigFin (Jul 2018) the company had raised £2.5m in total, but round labels/investors are not published (Nettuno Capital and Simula Innovation reported as later investors, Dec 2019, undisclosed). Total not attributable to labelled equity rounds, so amount_raised left blank.

name: Traderion
description: Simulation based assessment and training tool for trading professionals.

grants.name: Romania Operational Programme Competitiveness 2014-2020 (ERDF co-financed)

funding_notes: Traderion (traderion.com), Romanian interbank trading simulator for training/assessing bank traders (founders Florin Cioacă, Florin Grosu; operated by Bold Technologies). Got €75k from Seedcamp (Sep 2015) after a few tens of thousands of dollars from US angels and ~€100k founder investment; a seed round was planned for 2016 but none was reported. 2017 EU/ERDF-cofinanced Romanian grant (amount not in primary source; Dealroom cites ~$750k).

name: UiPath
description: Leaders in Robotic Process Automation
funding_notes: UiPath (uipath.com), robotic process automation leader (Romanian-founded, now NYC HQ). Private equity rounds Seed through Series F sum to ~$1.95B (TechCrunch: ~$2B raised pre-IPO); Series F at $35B post-money. IPO'd on NYSE (PATH) April 2021 (~$1.34B offering, part secondary) — IPO excluded from total. Acquired fellow Seedcamp company Re:infer in 2022.

name: Medefer
description: Consultant advice at your fingertips
funding_notes: Medefer (medefer.com), UK CQC-regulated virtual outpatient provider for the NHS founded 2013 by Dr Bahman Nedjat-Shokouhi. £10m Series A led by Nickleby Capital (Sep 2020). Earlier Seedcamp-backed seed money (2015) and a reported £1.1m seed (Dec 2018) appear only in databases (Dealroom), not primary press, so excluded from total.

name: Land Insight
description: Find and assess off-market development land.
funding_notes: Land Insight (land.tech) rebranded to LandTech (Land Technologies Ltd) in 2019; LandInsight remains its site-sourcing product. £350k seed (2015) incl. Seedcamp and Pi Labs; JLL Spark ~£2.5m (Jan 2020, 'understood' figure per Property Week); £42m Series A led by Updata Partners (Oct 2021). CIBC Innovation Banking £10m growth capital (Feb 2023) is debt and excluded.

name: Curve
description: Building a money hub where you can spend, see, & save your money effortlessly, all in one place.
funding_notes: Curve (curve.com), London card-aggregation 'money hub' fintech (founder Shachar Bialick) — not Curve Fitness. Company stated £208m equity raised to date (Sep 2023), with Series C totalling >£133m; amount_raised uses that company figure (individual rounds mix USD/GBP). Lloyds Banking Group agreed to acquire Curve (~£120m reported) in Nov 2025; completion reported mid-2026.

name: Branchtrack
description: The effective way to boost sales and customer care skills
funding_notes: BranchTrack (branchtrack.com), Riga-founded scenario-based training simulation builder. Seedcamp invested Dec 2014 (undisclosed); €250k seed round Mar 2016 from Imprimatur Capital, Coffee Ventures and Zbigniew Gulbinowicz. Also won $10k How To Web 'Best Startup' prize (2015, not counted). No later rounds reported.

name: Reinfer
description: Re:infer takes the communications streams you receive and turns them into something you can automate a business process against.
funding_notes: Re:infer (reinfer.io), UCL AI-lab spinout (2015) turning business communications into structured data. $3.5m (£2.5m) seed led by Touchstone Innovations (Feb 2018); company announced $7.6m raised to date in Feb 2022 alongside a ~£3.2m seed follow-on led by Crane (some reports date a Crane-led ~$4.5m round to 2020 — likely the same money). amount_raised uses the company's $7.6m cumulative figure; TechCrunch later said 'a little more than $11m'. Acquired by UiPath Aug 2022 (undisclosed).

name: Grover
description: Reinventing consumption with a simple, on-demand subscription model for all the products you love.

investors: Mirae Asset-LG Electronics New Growth Fund

notable_investors: Mirae Asset-LG Electronics New Growth Fund
funding_notes: Grover (grover.com, formerly ByeBuy), Berlin consumer-tech rental/subscription platform. Equity-only figures listed; excludes large debt facilities (€25m 2018, €30m Varengold 2019, €15m Kreos 2021, $220m Fasanara 2022, etc.; company cites >€1.4bn total financing incl. debt). Series C valued it >$1bn. 2024 €50m 'bridge' instrument type not specified (may be convertible). 2025 court-backed restructuring reportedly shifted majority equity to creditors. Mixed EUR/USD so amount_raised blank (~€119m + $110m).

name: Monese
description: Monese is a digital banking option that provides mobile-only, multi-currency accounts in countries across the European Economic Area.
funding_notes: Monese (monese.com), London/Estonian-founded mobile banking app (founder Norris Koppel). Totals reported: $15.8m after Series A (2017), $76m after Series B (2018), $162m after Series C first close (2021), $208m after HSBC's $35m (2022) — amount_raised uses that reported $208m cumulative (includes early seed/crowd money). Series C reported as $90m by TechCrunch (£65.8m headline by Deal Lite). Acquired in a rescue deal by Pockit in Oct 2024 (HSBC wrote off its stake).

name: Spoke
description: Properly made clothes that really fit, direct from the workshop.
funding_notes: Spoke (spoke-london.com), London D2C menswear/trousers brand (founder Ben Farren) — not Spoke messaging. $1.8m late seed (Jan 2017; total then just over $3m incl. earlier Seedcamp-era money); €9.7m (~£8.5m) Series B led by BGF (Oct 2019); £5m 2022 round mostly Seedrs crowdfunding (£4.71m from 1,579 investors) plus existing VCs. A £4m Nov 2017 Series A appears only in databases. Mixed USD/EUR/GBP so amount_raised blank.

name: Trussle
description: Simpler way to get a mortgage.
funding_notes: Trussle (trussle.com), London online mortgage broker (founder Ishaan Malhi). £1.1m seed (2016), £4.5m Series A (2017), £13.6m Series B (2018), £7.5m 2020 raise with Rabo Frontier Ventures (round label not stated; recorded here as Series B extension). Acquired by Better (Better.com) announced July 2021; trussle.com later rebranded to Better.co.uk.

name: Revolut
description: Revolut is a financial services company that specializes in mobile banking, card payments, money remittance, and foreign exchange.
funding_notes: Revolut (revolut.com), London-founded global fintech/'superapp' (CEO Nik Storonsky). Seedcamp invested Feb 2015; seed £1.5m ($2.3m) led by Balderton (Jul 2015), extended to $4.8m total by Feb 2016. Primary equity Series A–E sums to ~$1.71B (Series E at $33B). Later 2024 ($45B) and Nov 2025 ($75B, led by Coatue/Greenoaks/Dragoneer/Fidelity) transactions were employee/secondary share sales and excluded; Crowdcube campaigns folded into the Series A figure.

name: Marcopolo Learning
description: Reimagining children's media
funding_notes: New York-based MarcoPolo Learning (marcopololearning.com) makes early-childhood education apps and video. Raised ~$1M from angels in May 2013 (SEC Form D shows $740K sold of a $2M offering, first sale 2013-05-31), then an $8.5M round in April 2017 led by Boat Rocker Ventures with Horizons Ventures, Seedcamp and DST Global partners; ImpactAlpha labels it Series A (VentureBeat/FinSMEs call it its first round).

name: Hubble
description: Making renting office space easy
funding_notes: Hubble (hubblehq.com, legal entity Spacious Ltd, formerly Spacious/HubbleHQ) is a London flexible-office marketplace founded 2014 by Entrepreneur First alumni; not the telescope or Hubble Network. Rounds: £500K seed (2014, Spire lead, Seedcamp), £1.2M (2017), €4.6M Series A (2019, JLL Spark lead), £2M Series A follow-on (2021, Pi Labs lead); company said total raised £10M by July 2021. Mixed GBP/EUR so amount_raised left blank; a 2022 ~£7-8M round appears only in databases (not included). Acquired by Yardi in January 2025.

name: Property Partner
description: Property crowdfunding platform and trading exchange.
funding_notes: Property Partner (propertypartner.co) was a London residential property crowdfunding platform with a share-trading exchange, founded by Daniel Gandesha. Raised £150K angel (Feb 2014), £1.25M seed led by Octopus with Seedcamp (Sep 2014), £5.2M Series A led by Index Ventures (Mar 2015), and a £15.9M Series B led by Octopus with Index and Dawn (Mar 2016). The Series B included a £3M SVB venture-debt facility, so it's recorded as £12.9M equity; total equity is ~£19.5M (reported total funding £22.5M including debt).

name: Lodgify
description: Create your own vacation rental website
funding_notes: Lodgify (lodgify.com) is a Barcelona-based vacation-rental website/booking SaaS founded 2012 by Dennis Klett and Marco De Gregorio. Raised €1.4M in April 2016 led by Nauta (total €2M at that point, so ~€0.6M earlier from angels incl. HOWZAT/Hitchen/Zeller) and a $5M Series A in July 2018 (total $7.3M per TechCrunch). Mixed EUR/USD so amount_raised left blank; total reported $7.3M.

name: Reedsy
description: A community of top publishing professionals to create amazing books.
funding_notes: Reedsy (reedsy.com) is a London marketplace connecting authors with vetted editors, designers and marketers. Got €30K from Seedcamp and DC Thomson in 2014 while raising a €500K round; TechCrunch (Apr 2015) reported an undisclosed 'initial round of financing' with DN Capital, Kima, DC Thomson, Seedcamp and angels, not labelled seed. A ~€1.1M EU (EIC/SME Instrument) grant in 2016 appears only in a database and is not included as unverified.

name: BridgeU
description: Data-driven university and careers guidance to empower schools
funding_notes: BridgeU (bridge-u.com) is a London university and careers guidance platform for international schools, founded by Lucy Stonehill and Hywel Carver; Seedcamp backed it in spring 2014. Raised a $2.5M seed (Nov 2015, Octopus lead) and a $5.3M/£4M Series A (Oct 2017, Octopus lead). Acquired by Kaplan (agreed March 2020, announced Jan 2021, undisclosed) and later by Manifest Global (2025).

name: Satago
description: Helping businesses get paid on time.
funding_notes: Satago (satago.com) is a London invoice-finance and credit-control platform for SMEs; TruFin plc is its majority owner. Raised £30K on Seedrs, a $1M 'second round' in May 2014 (E-merge, BDMI, Ed Wray, William Reeve), and £1.6M equity from ESF Capital in June 2016 alongside a £3M credit line (debt, excluded), plus £550K from previous investors. Lloyds took a 20% stake for £5M in March 2022 (£20M pre-money). Reputable sources never give these equity rounds a stage label (some databases call the 2016 deal a Series A), hence unclear-round-type. Mixed USD/GBP; GBP equity is ~£7.18M plus $1M.

name: Oradian
description: Oradian provides a unique enterprise solution to financial institutions across South East Asia and Africa.
funding_notes: Oradian (oradian.com) is a Zagreb-based cloud core-banking (Instafin) provider for microfinance institutions in Africa and the Philippines. TechCrunch reported an undisclosed seed round in May 2015 (Credo, Playfair, Day One, Esther Dyson, Africa Angels Network); Seedcamp is named as another seed investor. A $2.1M Series A (July 2016, Rivers Capital Partners lead, with Finance in Motion) comes from Poslovni dnevnik, which itself cites a database, so treat the amount with caution. Feb 2018 investments from Middleton Enterprises (~100K, currency garbled in source) and Goodwell were undisclosed. Total unknown, so amount_raised is blank.

name: Elliptic
description: Identifying illicit activity on the blockchain

funding_rounds.stage: Funding round (unlabelled; databases list as Seed)

funding_notes: Elliptic (elliptic.co) is a London blockchain analytics / crypto compliance company founded 2013 that joined Seedcamp in Feb 2014. Raised $2M from Octopus (Jul 2014), $5M Series A led by Paladin (Mar 2018), a Series B that opened at $23M led by SBI (Sep 2019) and grew to $28M with Wells Fargo Strategic Capital (May 2020), and a $60M Series C led by Evolution Equity with SoftBank Vision Fund 2 (Oct 2021). Total ~$95M.

name: Tanaza
description: All-in-one software that turns common Wi-Fi routers into cloud-managed Wi-Fi social hotspots.

grants.name: European Commission (Horizon 2020 SME Instrument Phase 2 / EIC)

funding_notes: Tanaza (tanaza.com) is a Milan-based cloud Wi-Fi management software company (Tanaza SpA). Early financing came from Italian investment firm OrmaPrima; it joined Seedcamp in Feb 2014. A '€500K seed led by Seedcamp' figure appears only in aggregator databases and is not confirmed by reputable press. Got a €1.62M Horizon 2020 SME Instrument grant (signed Jul 2019); Il Sole 24 Ore (Aug 2019) said a third-party investor might come in within 6-12 months, but no later priced round was found.

name: Fishbrain
description: The fastest growing app & social network for the world's biggest hobby - sport fishing
funding_notes: Fishbrain (fishbrain.com) is a Stockholm-based fishing app, social network and marketplace that won Seedcamp Berlin in 2013. Rounds: $150K seed (2013), $2.4M pre-Series A (2014, Northzone/Active), $8M Series A (2015, Northzone), $13.5M Series B (2018, B Capital; TechCrunch said total $28M by then), and an unlabelled $31M round (Mar 2021). A 2022 Republic SPV listing (withdrawn) describes a $20M Series C at a $70M pre-money valuation; that close isn't independently confirmed, so its amount is not counted. amount_raised sums the listed rounds; TechCrunch's total implies ~$59M including earlier undisclosed money.

name: Countly
description: Mobile analytics for the enterprise
funding_notes: Countly (countly.com) is an open-source, self-hosted product analytics platform founded by Onur Alp Soner. It was picked at Mini Seedcamp Istanbul in 2013 and joined Seedcamp (undisclosed micro-investment), but the CEO says it has been bootstrapped and took no outside VC. A '£830K seed led by Seedcamp' on StartupHub.ai mixes it up with London-based Count (Sifted, May 2026) and is excluded.

name: Codacy
description: Automating code reviews and monitors code quality over time.
funding_notes: Codacy (codacy.com) is a Lisbon-based automated code review / code quality platform that went through Seedcamp. Raised a €1M ($1.1M) seed extension in Oct 2015 led by Caixa Capital (total €1.5M then, so ~€0.5M in earlier undisclosed seed money), a $5.1M Series A in Aug 2017 led by EQT Ventures with Seedcamp, and a $15M Series B in Sep 2022 led by Bright Pixel. amount_raised ($21.2M) leaves out the earlier ~€0.5M.

name: James Finance
description: Predict bad loans with Machine Learning. Based on the best machine learning algorithms, James helps Risk Officers generate highly predictive credit scoring models.
funding_notes: James (james.finance, formerly CrowdProcess) was a Lisbon/New York credit-risk ML startup founded 2011 by João Menano, Pedro Fonseca and Sam Hopkins; Seedcamp invested after Seedcamp Lisbon in Nov 2012. In June/July 2017 it raised $2.7M (€2.5M), led by ex-Credit Suisse board member Gaël de Boissard with Henry Ritchotte and BiG Start Ventures; sources don't give it a stage label. Reportedly acquired by Google in January 2019 (database/Portuguese press; terms undisclosed).

name: Codeship
description: A fast and secure hosted Continuous Delivery platform that scales with your needs.
funding_notes: Codeship (codeship.com) was a hosted CI/CD platform founded in Vienna in 2011 by Moritz Plassnig, Manuel Weiss and Florian Motlik, later based in Boston (Techstars Boston alum). Raised $2.6M in Feb 2014 led by Sigma Prime (unlabelled in VentureBeat) and a $7M Series A in July 2016 led by Ascent Venture Partners (total $11.1M per Business Wire, so ~$1.5M earlier money is undisclosed). CloudBees acquired it in Feb 2018, terms undisclosed.

name: Minubo
description: eCommerce Intelligence in the Cloud. Your online shop’s data hub with all key metrics
funding_notes: minubo.com (minubo GmbH), Hamburg, Germany; e-commerce BI SaaS, founded 2013, opened Boston office (minubo Inc.) in 2014. €1M seed Sep 2013 (Seedcamp, Tola Capital, HTGF + e-commerce angels) per TechCrunch/HTGF; second seed Dec 2014 described only as 'seven-digit', led by Stephan Schambach with Seedcamp, HTGF, Tola (EU-Startups/HTGF). Total left blank because second round amount is undisclosed (at least ~€2M combined). No later equity round found in reputable sources; trackers mention later debt/secondary only.

name: Hole19
description: Building the most amazing user experience for golfers on the course!

grants.name: Prémio Nacional de Indústrias Criativas (Fundação de Serralves / Unicer)
QREN (Portuguese national strategic framework) funding

funding_notes: hole19golf.com, Lisbon, Portugal; golf GPS/scorecard app founded 2011 by Anthony Douglas; Seedcamp 2013. Forbes Portugal: White Star Capital and e42 invested €170k after Seedcamp (2013); second round 2014 with Faber Ventures of 'close to €300k' (amount left null as approximate); founder also used family/friends money, a €25k creative-industries prize and applied for €500k QREN funding (QREN grant receipt implied, not explicitly confirmed). Observador later cited ~€2.2M invested by Faber, Caixa Capital, White Star, e42, Seedcamp and angels. The Aug 2017 ~€3.47M round (Caixa Capital, Kibo, White Star, Faber) is sourced only from tracker-style sites (bouncewatch/indexed; amounts vary $1.7M–$4.1M) — no reputable press article found. White Star Capital lists Hole19 as an active portfolio company. Total left blank given conflicting/approximate figures.

name: SimpleTax
description: The smart self assessment tax return filing software
funding_notes: gosimpletax.com (GoSimpleTax), UK self-assessment tax filing software. Original SimpleTax was founded by Portuguese CEO Celso Pinto, attended Seedcamp Week London Sep 2012 and got Seedcamp funding (accelerator check, amount undisclosed), launched in UK Jan 2013 (TNW). A ~£150k Dec 2012 seed appears only on tracker sites. Caveat: AccountingWEB describes today's GoSimpleTax as founded 2016 by the team behind Keytime, so ownership appears to have changed hands (transfer not publicly documented). Only public financing found: £250k DEBT from NPIF – FW Capital Debt Finance (Oct 2022) — debt, not equity, so not counted. GoSimpleTax acquired Coconut (bookkeeping app) in 2023. No priced equity round found.

name: SayDuck
description: Add reality to your sales
funding_notes: sayduck.com, Helsinki, Finland (office in Vilnius); 3D/AR product visualization for e-commerce, founded 2012. ArcticStartup: €350k seed (Jan 2014) from IncubAsia Ventures, Arteel Ventures and angels; another €350k (Nov 2014) led by Arteel. ~€1.2M total incl. Seedcamp €50k and a €450k 2013 round per Tech.eu Funding Explorer (data product; 2013 round not confirmed in a news article). ACQUIRED by Bublar Group (Sweden) July 2019 for SEK 13.5M paid in newly issued Bublar shares plus an earn-out (Cision). Later part of Goodbye Kansas Group; Dealroom says it partnered with The Optical Foundry in 2024 (unverified).

name: Antavo
description: Contest and loyalty software for e-commerce and retail brands
funding_notes: antavo.com, London-registered with HQ/engineering in Szeged, Hungary; enterprise loyalty cloud SaaS (clients BMW, KFC, BrewDog). €10M Series A Nov 2022 led by Euroventures with Lead Ventures, iEurope, Innovation Nest and angels (PR Newswire/Tech.eu). EIB story: €1.3M investment from Innovation Nest in 2018 (iEurope reportedly co-invested; seed label from trackers). Total €11.3M = sum of these two sourced rounds; small earlier Seedcamp/angel rounds (2012-2016) are undisclosed. Company said in Sep 2024 it was preparing a Series B for 2025; no completed Series B found.

name: 24Symbols
description: Read digital books online
funding_notes: 24symbols.com, Madrid, Spain; 'Spotify for ebooks' subscription reading platform founded 2010, Seedcamp portfolio. May 2013: mobile content group Zed bought a 32% stake for €2M (implied €6.25M valuation) alongside a distribution deal (TNW, independently confirmed; madri+d). Stage never named — a corporate strategic minority investment, hence unclear-round-type. An earlier ~€250k round is mentioned only in secondary coverage (El Cronista), not counted. Status today uncertain: site/apps still up, but Draft2Digital removed 24symbols distribution in Jan 2021 citing operational/payment problems — possibly dormant.

name: Qminder
description: Qminder is a cloud-based queue management system.

investors: angels from Toggl, Veriff, Pipedrive, Wise, Twilio

notable_investors: angels from Toggl, Veriff, Pipedrive, Wise, Twilio
funding_notes: qminder.com, Tartu, Estonia; queue/service-flow management SaaS founded 2011 (Garage48 origin), Seedcamp-backed 2012, then ~10 years profitable bootstrapping (small 2014 angel investment from Astrec Invest per trackers, undisclosed). €3M seed Nov 2024 led by Practica Capital with Jaan Tallinn's Metaplanet, BADideas.fund and angels — described by the company as its first institutional funding (Qminder blog, Tech.eu). Total reflects only this round.

name: Wise
description: Send money abroad easily and quickly with low-cost transfers
funding_notes: wise.com (Wise plc, formerly TransferWise), London; founded 2011 by Taavet Hinrikus and Kristo Käärmann; Seedcamp was a pre-seed/seed investor (sold its stake by 2017). Sourced rounds: $6M Series A 2013 (Valar), $25M Series B 2014 (Branson), $58M Series C 2015 (a16z), $280M Series E Nov 2017 (Old Mutual GI + IVP, ~$1.6B valuation, partly secondary). TechCrunch: total raised $397M as of Nov 2017 (includes a 2016 Series D not itemized here, and some secondary). Later 2019/2020 rounds were largely secondary share sales and not counted. PUBLIC: direct listing on the London Stock Exchange 7 Jul 2021, ~£8.75B (~$11B) valuation (Reuters/CNBC).

name: Holvi
description: Banking for makers and doers
funding_notes: holvi.com, Helsinki, Finland; online business banking for freelancers/SMEs founded 2011, Seedcamp-backed. €1M round May 2014 led by Speedinvest (its first Nordic deal) to expand to Austria/Ireland (ArcticStartup/Finovate) — labelled seed by trackers. Tech.eu: ~€2M raised in total before ACQUISITION by BBVA (Mar 2016, terms undisclosed). BBVA sold Holvi in Feb 2021 to Keru Fintech Investments, a vehicle of co-founder Tuomas Toivonen (management buyback); profitable by 2023. Dealroom lists additional small 2011-2015 rounds (€300k-€2.5M) not confirmed in press; total uses Tech.eu's ~€2M figure.

name: Grabcad
description: GrabCAD is an online community network for mechanical engineers to share talent, expand knowledge and collaborate with others.
funding_notes: grabcad.com, Boston (Estonian roots/dev office in Tallinn); online CAD community and collaboration platform. TechCrunch Oct 2012: $8.15M Series B led by Charles River Ventures with David Sacks and existing Atlas, NextView, Matrix; prior $1.1M seed and $4M Series A (dates not given there); TC says ~$14M total — $13.25M is the sum of the three disclosed rounds. ACQUIRED by Stratasys (all-cash, closed 23 Sep 2014; ~ $100M reported, terms not officially disclosed). Now part of Stratasys.

name: Profitero
description: Global Online Insights for Retailers and Brands
funding_notes: profitero.com, founded 2010 in Dublin (Dún Laoghaire), Ireland, offices in Boston/NY/London etc.; e-commerce analytics. $8M Series A Jun 2014 from Polaris Partners (TechCrunch/company PR); $20M Series B Apr 2020 led by Scaleworks with Conviction Capital (Irish Times/company PR). Irish Times: total 'more than $30M' including ~$9M from Polaris + Silicon Valley Bank and ~$1M early seed from Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland — amount_raised uses that $30M floor. ACQUIRED by Publicis Groupe May 2022 for €200M (Reuters).

name: EDITED
description: The world’s biggest apparel data warehouse.
funding_notes: edited.com, London (also Dallas, Sofia); retail intelligence/apparel data SaaS founded 2009 by Geoff Watts and Julia Fowler. $29M round Apr 2020 led by Wavecrest Growth Partners and Beringea UK with Hermes, bringing total to $34M (VentureBeat); $15M growth round Mar 2023 led by Delta-v Capital (company press, Tech.eu). Total $49M = $34M + $15M. Round labels are 'growth'; no Series letter published.

name: Scoville
description: A location-based recommendation engine that helps users discover at least one new place in their town each week
funding_notes: goscoville.com (also scoville.com), London; location-discovery app built on Foursquare check-ins (#TopTuesday), pivoted from travel startup Kukunu; founders Gerald Goldstein and Itamar Lesuisse. TechCrunch Apr 2011: 'recently raised $400K in funding from Seedcamp, Kima Ventures, and Jaina Capital', called seed funding — small and round terms (priced vs convertible) unknown; includes the Seedcamp check, so seed+ is borderline. No later funding or activity found; appears DEFUNCT (domain could not be confirmed live).

name: Erply
description: Web based affordable point of sale software and inventory system for retailers
funding_notes: erply.com, Estonia (Tallinn) with US presence (NYC sales office in 2013); cloud POS/inventory software for retailers, CEO Kristjan Hiiemaa. $2M Mar 2010 from Redpoint, Index Ventures and angels (TechCrunch, Ärileht); $2.15M Series B May 2013 led by Redpoint with Index and 500 Startups, TechCrunch says total VC $4.2M (sum of disclosed rounds $4.15M; small early Seedcamp ~€50k 2009 check not counted). A ~€50k EU Horizon 2020 SME grant (2016) is mentioned only by trackers, not included. No later round found; company still operating.

name: Codility
description: Codility is an automated tool for assessment of programming skills.
funding_notes: Codility (codility.com; Codility Limited, Companies House 07048726), Warsaw-founded technical-skills assessment platform with London/San Francisco offices. Seedcamp 2009 winner (EUR 50k for a 5-10% stake), then bootstrapped for ~10 years before a $22M Series A in Jan 2020 co-led by Oxx and Kennet Partners. Companies House SH01 shows Series B preferred shares allotted for cash 4-14 Jul 2022 totalling ~GBP 28.9M (computed from shares x price paid); investors and any press announcement for this Series B were not found, so investors are left empty. amount_raised left blank because rounds are in mixed EUR/USD/GBP (~$22M + ~GBP 28.9M + EUR 50k).

name: Platogo
description: Gaming studio

grants.name: departure (Vienna city creative-industries funding programme)

funding_notes: Platogo (platogo.com), Vienna-based browser/social game portal and studio (launched Sept 2009, user-generated game levels). Seedcamp invested via a Mini Seedcamp event in 2009 (amount undisclosed, per TechCrunch); the Guardian reports funding from departure, Vienna city council's entrepreneurial fund (treated as public funding/grant, amount undisclosed). No priced seed or VC round found. Later became a subsidiary of Greentube (Novomatic's interactive division), per Greentube's own publications; the ~2013 acquisition date comes only from trackers.

name: Patients Know Best
description: Patients Know Best provide hospitals with personal health records software so that their patients can better manage their health
funding_notes: Patients Know Best (patientsknowbest.com), Cambridge/London UK patient-controlled personal health record platform (founder/CEO Dr Mohammad Al-Ubaydli), B Corp. Seedcamp 2009 winner (EUR 50k). Raised $1.7M led by Maxfield Capital (Nov 2014; company later called it GBP 1m), GBP 3.5m led by Balderton Capital (Dec 2015), an undisclosed equity round led by OMRON Ventures with Balderton (Jun 2019) and an undisclosed strategic minority investment from DNV Ventures (Sep 2025). None of these is given a seed/Series label in primary or reputable sources (trackers label 2019 a Series A), hence unclear-round-type even though they are VC-led. A GBP 6m facility from Growth Lending (reported by Digital Health) is a loan and is excluded from rounds and totals. amount_raised blank: mixed EUR/USD/GBP and two undisclosed rounds.

name: toksta
description: Highly scalable instant messenger and chat solutions for online communities
funding_notes: toksta (toksta.com), Berlin/Potsdam white-label instant messaging and webcam chat for online communities, founded late 2007 by Felix Fidelsberger and Michael Gloess; later renamed stickapps. Seedcamp 2008 winner (EUR 50k) and also backed by Team Europe Ventures (amount and round type undisclosed). Sold in Dec 2009 to Roman Szubryt (owner of Polish dev shop Mainseek), per deutsche-startups.de; terms undisclosed. The domain is now defunct. amount_raised shows the disclosed Seedcamp EUR 50k only.

name: stupeflix
description: Make beautiful videos online, easily
funding_notes: Stupeflix (stupeflix.com), Paris-based online/mobile video creation company (Stupeflix Studio, API, Replay and Steady apps). Seedcamp 2008 winner (EUR 50k); TechCrunch (Jul 2014) says it had 'barely raised money', from Seedcamp and 500 Startups (500 Startups amount, date and round type undisclosed; trackers date it to Nov 2012 alongside Andurance Ventures and angels, not confirmed in reputable sources). GoPro acquired Stupeflix and Vemory in Feb 2016 for $105M combined (cash and stock). amount_raised shows the disclosed Seedcamp EUR 50k only.

name: Evercontact
description: Your contacts automatically up to date

investors: Private investors advised by Financiere Fonds Prives

notable_investors: Private investors advised by Financiere Fonds Prives
funding_notes: Evercontact (evercontact.com), Paris-based service that extracts contact details from email signatures to keep address books/CRMs up to date; built by Kwaga (formerly WriteThat.Name). Seedcamp invested via a Mini Seedcamp in 2009 and Kima Ventures also provided early seed money (amounts undisclosed). Raised a $1.55M Series A from private investors advised by Financiere Fonds Prives (Jan 2012) and $1M (~EUR 700k) from AXA Strategic Ventures (Apr 2015, AXA's first investment; stage unlabelled). amount_raised = disclosed USD rounds only ($1.55M + $1M).

name: Basekit
description: The most partner friendly site builder
funding_notes: BaseKit (basekit.com), Bristol/London-based white-label website builder sold through hosting and telco partners (founders Simon Best, Richard Best, Richard Healy). Seedcamp 2008 winner (EUR 50k); $2.6M Series A from Eden Ventures and NESTA (Jun 2010); $6.5M (~GBP 4M) from Nauta Capital, Eden and NESTA (Mar 2011); GBP 4.5m led by Angel CoFund (Feb 2014), which TechCrunch said brought the total to ~GBP 14.5m; and GBP 1m from existing investors (Mar 2022). That implies ~GBP 15.5m total, but amount_raised is left blank because the rounds mix EUR/USD/GBP. An undisclosed 2009 Eden/NESTA investment appears in secondary sources only.

name: Zemanta
description: Content Ads, Amplified & Optimized
funding_notes: Zemanta (zemanta.com), Ljubljana, Slovenia-founded company (later HQ'd in New York) that started as a blogging recommendation tool and became a native-advertising DSP (Zemanta One). Seedcamp 2007 winner. Seed money from Eden Ventures and The Accelerator Group, then Union Square Ventures added $650k in Sep 2008 (TechCrunch: $2.2M seed raised to that point from the three); $3M from USV and Eden (Nov 2010, ~$6M total); $2M from USV and Social Starts (Nov 2013). The company said it had raised $8M to date, which is used as amount_raised (Tech.eu later said 'more than $8 million'). A $1.6M Aug 2009 round appears only in trackers and is not itemised. Outbrain acquired Zemanta in Jul 2017 (undisclosed).

name: MyBuilder
description: Find trusted builders and tradesmen.
funding_notes: MyBuilder (mybuilder.com), London-based marketplace matching homeowners with vetted tradespeople, founded by former stonemason Ryan Notz (began as Buildersite in 2004). Seedcamp 2007 winner, then undisclosed angel money; profitable in 2008. Channel 4's 4iP fund bought a GBP 350k minority stake in Sep 2009 (not given a round label). IAC's HomeAdvisor acquired MyBuilder in Mar 2017 (terms undisclosed); Angi later raised its stake to 95% in 2021. amount_raised shows the disclosed GBP 350k only (Seedcamp and angel amounts undisclosed).

name: Lupin & Holmes
description: Offensive security for software supply-chain risk

investors: founders of Wiz, Hugging Face and GitGuardian (angels)

notable_investors: founders of Wiz, Hugging Face and GitGuardian (angels)
funding_notes: Lupin & Holmes (landh.tech), founded by bug bounty hunter Roni Carta, builds Depi for software supply-chain offensive security. Raised a $5.9M pre-seed (Tech.eu, 2026-03-17) co-led by 20VC and Seedcamp with Purple Fund, Kima Ventures and angel founders of Wiz, Hugging Face and GitGuardian. No seed or later round found.

name: Crowd.dev
description: Developer community data platform

investors: angels (Russ Heddleston, Cedric Sellin, Matthäus Krzykowski, Christian Stiebner)

notable_investors: angels (Russ Heddleston, Cedric Sellin, Matthäus Krzykowski, Christian Stiebner)
