name: C12 Quantum Electronics
description: C12 proposes a radically new approach to quantum hardware. Instead of scaling imperfect qubits (the basic units of quantum computers) and trying to compensate in the architecture, C12 uses material innovation to develop near-perfect building blocks first. It proposes ultrapure carbon nanotubes to trap single electrons which act as near-perfect spin qubits. C12 has the unique ability to manufacture these carbon nanotubes with the right dimensions and place them on a semiconductor chip. This approach and the purity of the material render the proposed hardware much more scalable than currently existing quantum computers, with drastically reduced error rates. Therefore, this novel approach could disrupt the nascent quantum hardware market which is poised to grow to a trillion-dollar industry in the coming years.

name: Case45
description: Case45 has developed an AI prognostication model that considers cancer ecology which measures a patient’s immune response to the tumor. The company relies on digital images of histology slides, which are standard for diagnosing cancer. It works with any type of lab machinery. Case45 will analyze the data (a typical slide will have more than 1 million cells of different types present) and return the results to the clinic in minutes. The algorithm considers various factors by identifying and counting different cell types and their spatial relations. One crucial element is the analysis of immune infiltration—how many immune cells are present in the tumor and adjacent to it? (Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes or TIL). Furthermore, the algorithm can detect the evolution history of the cancer by identifying “hot” and “cold” areas that are less or more infiltrated by immune cells.

name: CellVoyant
description: CellVoyant is an AI-first company developing closed-loop optimisation platforms for cell and tissue manufacturing based on their three products – FateView, FateCast, and FateSim. The products allow for label free identification, assessment, selection, prediction, and control of cell state and fate. The company so far has focused on induced Pluripotent Stem Cells (iPSCs). However, their end-to-end deep learning platform allows for generalisation across any cell types. The tech stack is composed of label free imaging and computer vision for cell identification with the key part of their techstack being the Bayesian Neural Networks that allow for time series analysis and quantification of all the physical and biological to steer the cells to a certain direction of interest. In other words, combining all three products, CellVoyant wants to develop autonomous driving of cell manufacturing.

name: Climeworks
description: Climeworks develops, builds and operates Direct Air Capture (DAC) machines to capture CO₂ directly from the air, with 15 machines currently in operation. The captured carbon dioxide can either be recycled and reused as a raw material or completely removed from the air by safely storing it underground, permanently. The raw material, pure CO₂ gas, is used by customers in industries such as commercial agriculture, energy, food and beverage and automotive, for uses such as carbonating drinks or for producing carbon-neutral hydrocarbon fuels and materials. By using Climeworks’ CO₂, customers can reduce their overall emissions as well as lowering their dependence on fossil energy.

name: Comphya
description: Comphya is developing an active implantable medical device to restore the erectile function of patient non-responsive to oral drugs (e.g. Viagra or Cialis). To achieve erection, these patients have to resort to intrapenial injections of vasodilators or penile implants, which are quite problematic and outdated. Thus, there is a clear need for better modalities for these patients. Comphya’s main focus is spinal cord injury (SCI) and prostatectomy patients.

name: CREAL
description: CREAL is developing a near-eye light-field display technology for Virtual and Mixed Reality headsets and smart glasses. The visual discomfort of today’s virtual and augmented reality glasses is holding back the entire industry. All current headsets provide incorrect 3D images with conflicting depth cues straining our eyes. CREAL’s patented near-eye display technology projects hologram-like images with correct depth cues that allow eyes to change focus naturally and without strain or nausea.

name: Cubbit
description: Cubbit is a cloud storage enabler (and not a storage provider – they do not own data centers). The company sells software to enterprises so that they can set up a cloud storage solution. The data is stored in a growing network of Cubbit’s partners’ data centers (and the client’s infrastructure). At the heart of Cubbit’s offering is encryption and geo-distribution of data. It applies a concept used in databases called sharding, which means partitioning something into smaller and more manageable parts.

name: Druid
description: Druid provides a low-code platform to build and deploy enterprise-grade conversational business applications consisting of a virtual assistant-based interface, automation functions, and AI-based capabilities (natural language understanding, machine learning, optical character recognition, robotic process automation, etc.). Customers from various industries such as banking, telecom, retail, healthcare, and energy are using Druid to automate processes and save money. Use cases are internal (such as an HR, helpdesk, procurement, legal, finance) or customer-facing (such as customer support, contact center automation, etc.). Other use cases not only optimize productivity or reduce cost but generate new business: lead management and capturing, offering, contract management. Druid provides pre-built solutions for the most common use cases and integrates them into all kinds of business applications as well as UiPath’s process automation robots.

name: EarlySight
description: EarlySight aims to reduce vision loss by enabling precise detection and better monitoring of eye diseases. The company develops high-performance eye imaging instruments empowering doctors to see disease impacts that are invisible with the standard of care.

name: Ecorobotix
description: ecoRobotix’ ultra-high precision spraying technology performs weeding operations in grassland and row crops. Using cutting-edge AI, its vision and computer systems detect and selectively spray the weeds with a micro-dose of herbicide. The centimeter-precise detection and spraying reduce the volume of herbicide used up to 95%, while ensuring crops are not sprayed, allowing a significant yield increase. In addition to weeding operations, the technology can also be used to selectively spray the crop with insecticides, fungicides, or fertilizers, with the ultimate goal of taking care of every crop in a field, plant-by-plant. By means of its multi-camera vision system, ecoRobotix’ two products – a tractor towed machine and an autonomous robot – detect weeds and spray them once they pass under its spraying tool.

name: Encosa
description: encosa redefines energy flexibility for the Commercial & Industrial (C&I) sector through battery power (1-5 MW systems), turning complex battery technology into a plug-and-play solution. Their core offering is an end-to-end platform that manages the entire value chain from sales and financing to installation, trading, and performance monitoring. This platform enables maximum savings by combining energy saving functionalities and energy trading opportunities on one battery. After strong growth stories for battery startups at the residential (5-10 kW systems) and utility scale (>100 MW), the C&I sector is the remaining link to enable energy flexibility in the future energy system.

name: Factor2Energy
description: Factor2 Energy is at the forefront of next-generation geothermal energy. The Siemens Energy spin-out is developing a system that uses CO2 instead of water or brine as the extraction fluid for geothermal power plants. CO2 is injected in natural underground reservoirs, where the surrounding rock heats it. Production wells extract the heated CO2 to drive turbines, generating electricity. The cooled and condensed CO2 is then re-injected into the reservoir, creating a closed loop.

name: Fashwell
description: Fashwell was a spin-off of ETH Zurich and closing the gap between seeing a product and finding a product in an online shop. With the app users take pictures of pieces of clothing. The intelligent software then finds similar articles in online shops. Fashwell was sold to a major tech company.

name: Ferroelectric Memory
description: DRAM and SRAM are the two most widely used memory technologies today. They are omnipresent in all electronic devices from data centers to laptops, mobile phones, and cars. However, as demands for higher memory capacities, faster access times, and lower costs continue to rise, DRAM and SRAM have begun to show their limitations. On top of that, they are both volatile memories. This means that they require power to retain data. This leads to high energy demands and unnecessary redundancy to protect the data. Ferroelectric Memory Company (FMC) was established in 2016 in Germany. It has developed a disruptive technology that uses a patented new material to offer a new type of memory: Ferroelectric Non-Volatile Random Access Memory (Fe-NVRAM). As fast as DRAM, but non-volatile, Fe-NVRAM retains data even when disconnected from power. This reduces energy consumption by 90%.

name: Firstbird
description: Firstbird, the digital employee referral program, connects people with jobs and companies worldwide with suitable candidates. With Firstbird, employees become brand ambassadors, and referrals become a company’s most successful recruiting channel. Firstbird reduces recruiting costs and saves time, all the while increasing the quality and productivity of hires. Some of the world’s biggest companies trust in Firstbird for their recruiting. The platform incorporates reward and appreciation features, social recruiting, employer branding, and automated communication for employees.

name: Flyability
description: Flyability is a Lausanne-based scale-up developing and selling drones to gather visual inspection data on industrial assets. Today, these inspections are still mostly carried out manually by workers who are put in dangerous situations by having to enter confined spaces or climb high up to assess the state of a certain asset. Flyability aims to send drones instead of humans to carry out these missions. Given the highly demanding environment in which they operate, the drones are surrounded by a cage to ensure collision tolerance, making them very robust for this type of mission.

name: Frontastic
description: Software-as-a-Service startup Frontastic offers a frontend for online retailers that gives them more flexibility than services such as Shopify, without the need for costly in-house software development. It is the perfect “head” for the “headless” software architecture trend. Frontastic improves agility because business people can change elements in webshops instantly without the need to wait for IT to implement changes. Customers such as the luxury watch shop Chronext, Universal Music and Germany’s oldest family firm Prym rely on Frontastic.

name: GotCourts
description: GotCourts is a social network for racket sports players and an online service for booking courts and coaches. It’s the first platform to provide everything a player needs in a single network. Whether you want to find a partner or a coach, book a court nearby, compete for a place on GotCourts’ leaderboards or simply track your progress, GotCourts is the go-to “virtual global club”. For sports facilities and clubs, GotCourts offers a court management system and a platform to engage with the racket sport community.

name: Groove Quantum
description: Groove Quantum is a Dutch startup specializing in scalable quantum computing technology. Founded in 2024 by Anne-Marije Zwerver and Nico Hendrickx, the company is a spinout from QuTech, a leading quantum research center in Delft, the Netherlands. Groove Quantum focuses on developing quantum processors using standard semiconductor processes, making them compatible with existing chip manufacturing techniques. Their uniqueness lies in using germanium, a material also used for the first transistors, to make the qubits. This approach aims to address the scalability challenges in quantum computing by enabling the production of large-scale, high-fidelity quantum processors. Specifically, compared to other approaches in spin qubits, germanium allows for much easier control of the qubits and a more reliable fabrication process, two factors that have hindered scaling of the field.

name: Haelixa
description: Nearly 50% of cashmere, organic cotton and other premium fibers sold in Europe are fake, even if raw material is covered by global standards and certifications. Haelixa offers a DNA-based traceability solution that helps brands verify material authenticity, trace product origins, and enhance supply chain transparency. Haelixa is a spin-off of ETH Zürich, founded in 2016, transforming product traceability with innovative DNA marking technology. Backed by the expertise of the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, they are now a globally recognized leader in supply chain transparency. Meanwhile, global brands trust Haelixa to verify authenticity at scale – C&A, one of Europe’s largest fashion retailers, has already traced over 16,800 tons of organic cotton using their technology.

name: Ikerian
description: Ikerian (formerly RetinAI) harnesses the power of machine learning to transform the way doctors detect eye diseases. Trained with a dataset of tens of thousands of patients provided by renowned eye clinics, Ikerian’s algorithms speed up the doctor’s workflow, help them organize digital health records and detect eye diseases with an accuracy of 98%. Ikerian’s software enhances the image quality of eye scanners to a point where it is as good as machines ten times more expensive.

name: Inositec
description: Inositec is pioneering the development of life-saving small molecule drugs based on inositol phosphate, a natural facilitator of diverse cellular functions. Using its broadly applicable technology to adjust the chemical and physical properties of inositol phosphate (IP6) analogs, Inositec is developing a novel class of drugs currently focusing on high-unmet medical needs related to calcification disorders. The lead compound INS-3001 is a cardiovascular calcification inhibitor in development for aortic valve stenosis. Inositec was founded in December 2015 based on the award-winning research of Dr. Mattias Ivarsson, Prof. Jean-Christophe Leroux and Prof. Bastien Castagner at ETH Zurich, Switzerland.

name: Insolight
description: Insolight has developed an integrated agrivoltaic system that replaces plastic tunnels and greenhouses with a static structure with translucent photovoltaic modules that have an adjustable optical layer. By combining agriculture and solar energy production, agrivoltaics drastically reduces the land use of large solar arrays while protecting crops, making them carbon neutral and producing clean energy. Insolight’s solution is based on certified hardware components and dedicated proprietary software, which pilots the systems and logs agronomic and electrical data.

name: InterAx Biotech
description: InterAx is a Swiss biotech and a spin-off from the ETH Zurich and Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI). The company has developed a unique drug discovery platform combining mathematical models and cell-based assays to analyze G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). This technology allows for the early prediction of a drug’s effects and side effects, enabling pharmaceutical partners to select the best possible candidates, reduce failure rates, and bring more effective medicines to market faster.

name: IRUBIS
description: Irubis is a Munich-based deep-tech company providing an innovative sensor solution for real-time bioprocess monitoring. Its patented mid-infrared technology allows biotech and pharma companies to continuously track critical process parameters directly in the bioreactor, eliminating manual sampling. This data-driven approach optimizes the manufacturing of biologics, ensuring higher yields, improved quality, and faster time-to-market.

name: Kandou AI
description: Kandou AI is a Swiss hardware company developing copper-based interconnects for high-performance computing. It has three product lines focused on within-package interconnects, out-of-package interconnects and electronic packet switches. Kandou AI recently underwent a large restructuring and pivot into AI interconnects, and is raising a growth round. The demand for longer, ultra-high-bandwidth interconnects is driving two paths: integrating photonics closer to the chip despite high costs, or extending the current copper standard. Kandou AI is pursuing the latter with its core Chord signaling technology. Unlike standard differential signaling (1 bit over 2 wires), Chord signaling transmits a group of bits as a single mathematical unit (e.g., 5 bits over 6 wires). This results in correlated signals that reduce noise, increase bandwidth, and lower power consumption, forming the basis of their Copper MIMO (Multiple Input, Multiple Output) technology.

name: Kipu Quantum
description: Kipu is a quantum software company developing a new type of compression algorithms that will enable quantum computers to become useful 3-5 years earlier than existing conventional approaches. Their solution can be widely implemented directly at quantum hardware level and can then be tailored to multiple use cases, allowing Kipu to address the needs of both hardware manufactures and end users. Kipu is already running proof of concept (PoC) projects with clients such as chemical producer BASF, the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and Spanish telecom operator MasMovil. With its technology, the company can shorten the required computation time 2x and increase 5x the success probability with 100x lowered hardware requirements.

name: kiutra
description: Kiutra has developed a cooling device that can cool down and keep samples at temperatures below -272 degrees without using the rare isotope Helium-3. A patented automatic sample changer allows users to perform test measurements at low temperatures up to 10 times faster than with conventional gas-cooled equipment. Sub-Kelvin temperatures are essential in fundamental research as well as in the developing quantum technology markets.

name: kyron.bio
description: Kyron Bio uses an innovative cell line engineering approach to unlock precision control of glycosylation patterns on therapeutic proteins. This breakthrough technology addresses several industry challenges, including reduction of antibody immunogenicity, enhancement of the drug’s half-life, and improvement in the antibody production QC process, to name a few. Furthermore, their platform could play a major role in optimizing the manufacturing of Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs) by enabling improved conjugation rates.

name: Lexroom AI
description: Lexroom.ai is redefining how lawyers work by harnessing the power of generative AI. The company’s platform offers advanced tools to streamline every stage of legal operations: from high-precision legal research and document analysis to automated drafting of legal briefs, contracts, and other documents.

name: Limula
description: Limula is a Swiss life science technology company on a mission to democratize cell and gene therapy. Addressing the critical manufacturing bottlenecks that limit patient access to treatments like CAR-T, Limula has developed a fully automated, closed platform for decentralized production. This end-to-end solution enables hospitals and clinical centers to produce personalized therapies at the point-of-care, dramatically reducing logistical complexity, costs, and vein-to-vein times. As a spin-off from the École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Limula is empowering its partners to scale their operations and bring life-saving treatments to more patients, faster.

name: Luminovo
description: To create an electronic product, developers need many off-the-shelf parts such as chips or diodes and a few custom parts specifically designed for the product. Many electronics developers do not produce these parts themselves but procure them from external part manufacturers and developers. They also often outsource assembly of the finished product. The process of procurement within this supply chain is currently done manually by employees. Luminovo aims to automate these processes at every level of the electronics supply chain by offering each stakeholder an easy to integrate Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) module that addresses their specific needs. Their ultimate goal is to create a platform that will cover the entire electronics development process end-to-end. They have already launched two modules: LumiQuote which streamlines quoting and procurement for electronics manufacturers and Stackrate that combines the visualization, analysis and adaptation of printed circuit boards in one tool.

name: medimaps
description: Medimaps’ software helps to better diagnose osteoporosis, a health condition that weakens bones and makes them more likely to break. The software provides a measure of bone quality by analyzing its microarchitecture. Medimaps is selling its software TBS iNsight for clinical use in more than 60 countries worldwide, and has already convinced more than 2’500 clinical centers as customers. TBS has gained international recognition with more than 720 peer-reviewed publications and is establishing itself as the standard of care by being integrated into official country osteoporosis guidelines, currently being in more than 20 guidelines. The software is pre-installed in the DXA devices of the two major manufacturers in this field (80% of the worldwide market) and has recently obtained very favorable reimbursement in the US.

name: MedTrace
description: MedTrace has developed a system that enables hospitals to produce and administer 15O-water on site. 15O-water is used as a tracer substance in PET scanners. MedTrace’s system includes proprietary imaging software that provides very clear images of the heart and allows doctors to diagnose coronary artery disease.

name: Memo Therapeutics
description: ETH spin-off Memo Therapeutics has developed a novel technology for rapid discovery of antibodies. Current methods to identify antibodies for drug development are based on investigating individual antibodies at a time and are very cost and time-intensive. Instead of focusing on one antibody at a time, Memo Therapeutics’ solution makes an individual’s entire antibody repertoire searchable and repeatedly accessible for drug discovery. This novel approach is 100-1000 times more efficient in finding rare antibodies for drug development. A landmark exit for European biotech: In 2026, Memo Therapeutics AG enters a definitive agreement to be acquired by global biopharma leader Ipsen for a total potential consideration in excess of €700 million, advancing first-in-class antibody potravitug toward pivotal trials for kidney transplant patients.

name: Metaco
description: Metaco enables secure custody of digital assets, an emerging trend that will revolutionize the financial world and goes far beyond cryptocurrencies. The robustness of Metaco’s solution is underlined by the fact that it is the first insurable digital asset management solution on the market, underwritten by insurance giant AON. Metaco’s product is integrated into the Avaloq core banking software.

name: Metafuels
description: Metafuels is developing an efficient, cost-effective production process for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from renewable resources. Their method uses water, renewable electricity, and sustainably sourced carbon dioxide to produce a high-quality aviation fuel that is compatible with existing jet engines and can both be blended into traditional fossil-based kerosene and become a primary fuel.

name: Multiomic Health
description: Multiomic is a next-generation precision medicine business, applying computational systems biology to develop and commercialize data assets for metabolic syndrome — the world’s largest healthcare burden. With our unique combination of data science and biology expertise, we are enabling data-driven development of therapeutics and are bringing understanding into complex biological systems. Metabolic syndrome, a cluster of closely-related diseases (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, non-alcoholic fatty liver) with many common risk factors, is costing the healthcare system $2 trillion (forecast >$5.5 trillion by 2040).

name: Nagi Bioscience
description: EPFL spin-off Nagi Bioscience has developed a device that allows rapid toxicology testing of new chemicals. It offers whole organism tests without falling under the animal test ban. The model organism, the 1mm worm C. elegans is introduced into the device on microfluidic chips. The device is able to measure different parameters for a large number of tests that run in parallel, a very effective and easy setup. Nagi sells its device to companies in the agrochemicals, cosmetics and pharma industries.

name: Ncodin
description: Ncodin is a French deep-tech company revolutionizing the semiconductor industry with its breakthrough optical interconnect technology. As traditional copper connections hit their physical limits, Ncodin’s solution, built on the world’s smallest laser integrated on silicon, shatters these barriers. The company’s plug-and-play optical interposer enables unprecedented data transfer speeds and energy efficiency within next-generation processors. This allows chipmakers to overcome the end of Moore’s Law and unlock the full potential of AI and High-Performance Computing (HPC). Backed by leading European deep-tech investors and founded on over 15 years of pioneering research, Ncodin is paving the way for the future of computation.

name: Neo Medical
description: Neo Medical has developed a Swiss-made toolset for spine surgery. Its ease of use has convinced surgeons. It reduces complexity, operating time, and the risk of infections. Instead of several hundred parts, it uses five instruments and fourteen implants only, and it still does a better job, potentially reducing risks of screw loosening, hardware failure, and eventually further reducing re-operation risks, while improving overall patient outcomes. To enhance safety, Neo’s screws and implants are sterile and single-use, which removes the need for sterilization in the hospital. This reduces the environmental footprint of spinal fusion surgery by 75% versus legacy reusable systems.

name: Neustark
description: neustark was founded in 2019 by Johannes Tiefenthaler and Valentin Gutknecht as an ETH Zurich spin-off. The two young entrepreneurs came together based on their shared vision of a solution for the utilization and storage of CO₂. In 2020, neustark’s first pilot plant was integrated into the production line of an established concrete producer. Today, various concrete producers store CO₂ with one of neustark’s mobile plants and produce concrete that is used both in private and public construction projects.

name: Once
description: Once uses a “slow dating” approach. Users have 24 hours to get in touch with a single daily match, generated by their state-of-the-art artificial intelligence technology.

name: ONWARD
description: “EPFL spin-off ONWARD is helping paralysed spinal cord injury patients regain important functions, thanks to groundbreaking neurostimulation technologies. Based on world-leading research, impressive pre-clinical results and a network of key opinion leaders, ONWARD has developed two platforms that use the same principle. They electrically stimulate the patients’ nerves to re-establish body functions that will help patients lead a more independent and improved life. Tests have shown that ONWARD’s technology promotes neuroplasticity, i.e. the stimulation leads to an improvement in movement patterns even after it is turned off. ONWARD is working to enable patients to move again, for some this might mean regaining basic functions to feed or dress themselves, for others, it could even mean resuming complex tasks such as walking or playing the guitar.

name: Optalysys
description: Optalysys is a UK-based deep-technology company at the forefront of photonic computing. The company develops and commercializes optical co-processing accelerators that perform complex calculations at a fraction of the time and energy cost of traditional silicon-based systems. Designed for seamless integration into data centres and high-performance computing (HPC) environments, Optalysys’s technology is unlocking new frontiers in computationally intensive fields. A primary focus is making Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) commercially viable, enabling secure, privacy-preserving computation on sensitive data for the finance, healthcare, and cybersecurity sectors. By delivering a step-change in processing capability, Optalysys is providing the critical infrastructure for the next generation of artificial intelligence and secure cloud computing.

name: Orakl Oncology
description: Orakl Oncology is a French biotechnology company at the forefront of precision oncology. The company has developed a proprietary platform that leverages patient-derived organoids, or “tumor avatars,” combined with advanced artificial intelligence to predict patient response to cancer treatments. By creating one of the largest and most diverse living tumor biobanks, Orakl provides deep, biologically relevant insights into drug efficacy. This empowers pharmaceutical and biotech partners to de-risk and accelerate their drug development pipelines, improve clinical trial design, and ultimately bring more effective, personalized therapies to the patients who need them most.

name: Orbex Space
description: Founded in 2015, Orbex is a UK-based orbital launch services company, serving the needs of the small satellite industry. The company has developed a microlauncher rocket that will be able to deliver 200kg of payload to orbit. The rocket uses 100% renewable fuel with 0% black carbon emissions and is largely reusable. Orbex designs and manufactures the whole rocket in-house and is also building its own dedicated launch site in Sutherland, Scotland. The Orbex team is highly experienced in the space industry, with their CTO, Jonas Bjarnoe, having worked on over 50 successful space missions for NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Danish space agency. Orbex is on track to become the first successful European microlauncher provider. The company is planning to launch its first rocket in 2023.

name: ORCA Computing
description: Orca Computing is a University of Oxford spin-off. It is developing quantum computing hardware based on light particles (photonics). Photonic quantum computers have some clear advantages. They use mostly existing telecom components for example and can run at room temperature without extensive infrastructure requirements. Furthermore, photons do not interact with the environment and are therefore much less sensitive to noise compared to other types of qubits. At the core of Orca’s technology is a patented quantum memory that allows it to trap and release photons on demand. This core innovation could be the answer to the fundamental challenge of optical quantum computing and therefore enable high-quality, scalable machines for a wide range of purposes.

name: Otoqi
description: Otoqi is a startup that solves two distinct problems with the same IT platform: handling the management of shared car fleets and delivering newly bought or leased vehicles to clients. With a first-mover advantage, Otoqi is in a unique position to build the leading automotive e-logistics platform in Europe. For more than 11 European car-sharing companies, Otoqi provides the backbone that handles all the mundane tasks such as car repositioning, servicing, refueling, recharging and cleaning. For car manufacturers such as BMW, Volvo and Daimler and leasing companies, it delivers cars from logistics hubs directly to the clients. This service allows bypassing car dealerships as pickup points. It is essential for brands that want to increase their share of online car sales.

name: PathoQuest
description: Identifying which bacteria or viruses have caused an infection is not straightforward with current methods. It takes several tests and several days, which in the context of hospitalized patients means it’s both expensive and slow. PathoQuest enables screening for more than 1200 pathogens with a single test instead of several. Patented blood sample preparation combined with bioinformatic processing and matching of results against a proprietary database make this breakthrough in diagnostics possible. PathoQuest’s CE-marked test significantly reduces the problematic use of broad-spectrum antibiotics. It is the major cause of antibiotic resistance, a growing danger to public health. PathoQuest scientific base is research by Prof. Marc Eloit, a world-leading virologist at Pasteur Institute in Paris.

name: Phlair
description: Phlair is developing a pioneering electrochemical direct air capture system. It removes CO2 from ambient air and industrial plants. Using standard components and patented technology, it uses less energy than competitors, which ultimately promises to lower costs to below USD 100 per ton. The process is also ideally suited to be combined with intermittent renewable energy sources such as wind and solar. Since its closed-loop mechanism splits a liquid into strong acids and basic solvents, these liquids can be stored as chemical energy storage. This means that the process can be powered by renewable electricity when available and cheap, unlike other DAC systems, which need constant electricity input.

name: Piomic
description: Chronic wounds are a widespread, growing phenomenon caused by an aging population and an increasing occurrence of diabetes. Wound care is an extremely large burden to healthcare systems, and has a huge impact on patients’ health and mental well-being. Direct medical cost, which includes treating wounds 2-3 times per week for months or years, is estimated to amount to up to USD 100 billion annually. The Swiss startup Piomic has developed an already CE-marked medical device that has been proven to promote the healing of chronic wounds that are difficult to treat and cause persistent pain to patients. Piomic’s COMS technology synergistically applies optical and magnetic stimulation externally to a wound. Its efficacy has been demonstrated in a clinical trial which showed a 2.5x accelerated wound healing rate. Piomic solution is the only one designed for home care and is highly cost-effective.

name: Poppins
description: Poppins has developed a breakthrough therapy based on 25 years of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies in neuropediatrics that uses Cognitive Music Therapy (CMT) to help children aged 7 to 11 struggling with these learning impairments. Designed as a fun mini game application, it has been proven to offer the equivalent of 1 year of normal neurological development for a child with learning impairments in just 2 months of use. Poppins’ solution also helps raise children’s self-confidence by automatically adjusting the level of the games based on their abilities. Levels remain challenging, but easy enough to pass without repeated failures.

name: Presentient
description: Conventional interim analyses are highly inefficient at finding the actual moment in a clinical trial where failure is inescapable or success conclusive. This costs the pharma industry $15bn+ in waste and delays. Presentient solves this with its breakthrough BRAKES platform which runs 20+ automated interim analyses while eliminating operational bias.

name: Puraffinity
description: The company has developed a novel platform technology that facilitates surface modification of a range of select substrates with tailored “PFAS-friendly” molecular groups. The result is a suite of adsorbent materials, exhibiting high selectivity towards diverse PFAS compounds adaptable for multiple applications. PFAS infiltration into groundwater requires a dedicated approach to enable effective remediation of polluted groundwater sites. Our adsorbents can be implemented easily, enabling retrofitting of existing assets if required. The highly selective PFAS adsorbent requires shorter Empty Bed Contact Times, leading to lower footprints and lower CAPEX. The flexibility of the solution enables application in diverse sites and scenarios.

name: QANT
description: Q.ANT is the photonic technology scale-up that emerged from TRUMPF’s R&D labs with deep knowledge in light generation, processing and detection. Since its founding as an independent startup in 2018, the company has been advancing and industrializing photonic and quantum technologies in computing and sensing, specialized in Native Computing and Native Sensing by Q.ANT, pushing the boundaries into new application areas and processes.

name: Qnami
description: Qnami manufactures quantum sensors that are able to measure magnetic fields at the nanoscale. The manufacturing of these sensors out of synthetic diamond is Qnami’s core competence. The company is developing a complete system consisting of a microscope, its quantum sensor and software to interpret the data. In a first step, the system is aimed at research laboratories and semiconductor manufacturers, allowing them for the first time to measure components at a nanoscale level. In the long-term, the technology is aimed to become applicable for industries such as medical imaging or automotive.

name: quitt.ch
description: The Internet platform quitt.ch offers private employers an intuitive online solution that saves time and hassle and ensures legally correct employments of domestic employees. Registration and set-up takes only 10 minutes: The employer has to provide his and the employee’s contact information, as well as some basic information on the employment such as salary and working hours.

name: Qumram
description: Qumram is a Big Data platform for compliant cross-channel recording, e-discovery and user experience intelligence. Online user behavior across all digital channels is an extremely valuable source of information for companies. In many industries, companies have a legal obligation to retain this information in its original form. With the Big Data platform from Qumram companies can record and analyze all of their customers’ online interactions while ensuring regulatory compliance.

name: Realxdata
description: RealXData’s goal is to make the commercial real estate asset class transparent and globally accessible for every investor by building the leading data driven analysis solution. Doing so, RealxData integrates proprietary data, utilises crowdsourced data and structures valuable public data.

name: S-Biomedic
description: The Belgian biotech startup S-Biomedic uses a proprietary technology to source and combine beneficial bacteria directly from healthy human skin to develop break-through treatments for skin conditions. This ensures that beneficial microbes colonize the skin in the most efficient way to rebalance the microbiome and ensure a long term and sustainable treatment.

name: Salonkee
description: Salonkee is an all-in-one software solution for hair and beauty salons that includes scheduling appointments, point-of-sales software, loyalty programs, and payments. It runs in the cloud and is easy to use for non tech-savvy salon owners. Salonkee focuses on the mid-market with salons that have a few employees and uses an in-field sales force to rapidly gain new customers.

name: Scrona AG
description: Scrona is transforming the semiconductor and electronics industries with its groundbreaking InkLogic™ printhead platform, which enables high-volume, sub-micron precision printing of circuits and components on virtually any 3D surface. This technology unlocks next-generation applications like AI interposers, advanced antennas, quantum dot microLEDs, and photonic devices. The platform’s unique, software-defined architecture provides unmatched versatility, making it compatible with nearly any liquid material for future-proof manufacturing. After unveiling the world’s first 128-nozzle InkLogic printhead at CES 2025, Scrona was named “Start-up of the Year” at the prestigious IEEE ECTC conference in June 2025. The company’s business model is based on partnering with capital equipment OEMs worldwide to integrate its printheads, which are consumable units that create a strong recurring revenue stream. As a venture-backed spin-out from ETH Zurich, its core electrohydrodynamic (EHD) technology is protected by numerous patents and holds the world record for printing the smallest full-color image ever created.

name: Seervision
description: The ETH spin-off Seervison fully automates multi-camera video production. This means that real-time events and hybrid online/studio events can be produced with much less effort and cost. Seervision’s image recognition software tracks people which allows robotic cameras to follow them. The system is able to create broadcast-quality videos in many different environments such as sport productions, conferences and remote television sets. This unrivaled technology allows production companies to significantly reduce costs and is already used by video production companies as well as large companies that produce video content in-house.

name: Sherpany
description: Sherpany is Europe’s leading software meeting management solution for corporate leadership meetings. It improves meeting efficiency. Its platform that allows online voting in assembly general meetings has shown significant growth over the last years and gained additional momentum as COVID-19 made large physical meetings impossible.

name: Sizable Energy
description: Sizable Energy is revolutionizing long-duration energy storage by adapting proven pumped hydro technology for offshore deployment. The company’s system uses a subsea reservoir on the ocean floor and a second floating on the surface, pumping saturated sea salt brine between them to store and release energy. This innovative approach unlocks unprecedented scalability and bypasses the geographical and land-use constraints of traditional methods.

name: Somagenetix
description: Somagenetix is a biotech company about to enter the clinical stage with next-generation precision gene therapy. Co-founder Janine Reichenbach, chaired Professor for Somatic Gene Therapy at the University of Zurich, and her team, leverage 15 years of world-class scientific and clinical expertise to disrupt this market with a novel technology platform. Somagenetix has the potential to become a next-generation breakthrough technology and a global leader in the field of blood cell (phagocyte) disorders. Phagocytes that do not function or function falsely play a crucial role in more than 50 diseases, ranging from immunodeficiencies, neurodegenerative disorders to cancers. Somagenetix’s technology platform allows for cell-specific expression, i.e. activation of genes only in specific targets, in this case, phagocytes.

name: Sympatient
description: Sympatient is building a proprietary operating system that turns psychotherapy delivery into a scalable system. It integrates coordinated access, operational execution, and structured quality/data systems – embedded directly into everyday clinical work. The result: a replicable delivery model for regulated care that expands capacity without compromising therapeutic standards and enables measurable performance uplift per practice.

name: TestingTime
description: Involving test users early in the design process is a key factor for companies to ensure that new products succeed in the market. However, it is expensive and time-consuming to recruit the right test users. With TestingTime, companies can order test users in less than 5 minutes and conduct user research 48 hours later–10 times faster than other solutions. TestingTime’s automated recruiting service integrates seamlessly into the product testing process. Several hundred companies including global firms such as UBS or Google have worked with TestingTime and recruited test users out of a pool of more than 500’000 individuals for usability tests, interviews, focus groups and online surveys.

name: Therapixel
description: Therapixel is a medical imaging startup. It has developed software that can easily detect, locate and characterize breast cancer on medical images using artificial intelligence. Their product, MammoScreen, is currently used as a reading aid by radiologists for tens of thousands of patients per month. Therapixel’s core technical asset is an algorithm trained on a dataset of over a million mammograms (x-ray pictures of breasts) labeled by trained radiologists. MammoScreen helps speed up the reading process by highlighting those cases that merit a closer look. It also reduces the frequency with which cancer cases are missed, which is very relevant for reducing the cost from malpractice litigation which is customary in the US. The software has received CE marking and FDA approval.

name: tozero
description: Currently, only 40% of EV batteries undergo some form of recycling, with the remaining 60% winding up in landfills. Existing recycling methods are highly inefficient and fail to recycle the black mass, which are the materials of the anode and cathode of the battery. tozero has developed a novel way of recycling Lithium-Ion Batteries (LiBs) based on the CTO’s ’s years of research and development experience at RWTH Aachen’s Institute for Process Metallurgy and Metal Recycling (IME). Through a proprietary process of hydrometallurgy or chemical leaching, tozero is able to recycle up to 97% of the Black Mass in LiBs and for the first time recover the valuable Lithium. After having conducted over 70 successful tests in a laboratory setting, tozero is now focusing on scaling its process, with the ambitious goal of building its first commercial size plant with a 30k tonnes capacity by 2030.

name: Transmutex
description: Transmutex is a nuclear energy pioneer with two business lines, producing life-saving medical isotopes as well as safe, carbon-free energy with a thorium reactor that “burns” legacy radioactive waste.

name: Turn2X
description: Turn Energy has developed a novel, efficient reactor to reduce the carbon footprint of heavy industry. It produces green methane, which is also called renewable natural gas (RNG) because it uses renewable energy. The process combines carbon dioxide (CO2) and hydrogen (H2) and produces RNG (methane, CH4) and water (H2O). Placed next to an industrial plant, this reactor effectively allows the plant to reduce the amount of carbon dioxide going into the atmosphere. Capturing CO2 and turning it into RNG which can then be used by the plant as source of energy again, this innovative technology allows for a circular production process.

name: Undecimal Bio
description: Undecimal Bio is a biotechnology company addressing the biggest bottleneck in genetic medicine: the inability to deliver RNA therapeutics (specifically siRNA) directly and efficiently to specific cells outside of the liver, where a delivery vehicle already exists, but where no other small molecule delivery vehicles have been discovered for the past 20 years. While delivery to the liver has already been solved, delivering these gene-silencing medicines is the next frontier.

name: Veesion
description: Veesion uses artificial intelligence and machine learning to prevent shoplifting in stores. The Veesion software runs on already installed cameras and analyzes gestures to detect possible theft without using facial recognition, and alerting employees via messages in real-time. The software is up to 20 times less expensive and catches 3 to 5 times more thefts than a security guard.

name: Verity
description: Verity is a Swiss-based robotics leader specializing in AI-powered autonomous indoor drone systems. Co-founded by Kiva Systems (exited to Amazon for $775million) pioneer Raffaello D’Andrea the ETH Zurich spin-off enables “zero-error warehouses” through fully autonomous, 24/7 inventory tracking for global giants like IKEA and Maersk.

name: Versantis
description: Versantis is a spin-off from ETH Zurich, Switzerland, developing a versatile antidote, capable of removing diverse toxic agents from the organism. Today, hospitals have no measure to deal with the acute form of cirrhosis. Using known and safe substances, the ETH spin-off has developed micro-capsules that trap ammonia and other toxins inside them. They will be applied in a procedure that these patients undergo in the hospital anyway.

name: WeMaintain
description: WeMaintain is an end-to-end B2B building operations platform. The startup is focused on the delivery of contractual elevator maintenance and fire & safety services. It combines a sleek IT platform with proprietary IoT sensors that are placed directly on the elevators and provide an actionable data set. WeMaintain has convinced some of Europe’s largest real estate owners such as Allianz, Swiss Life and BNP Paribas.

name: Wingtra
description: ETH spin-off Wingtra is the leading manufacturer of professional VTOL (vertical take-off and landing) drones for mapping and surveying. Its WingtraOne drone is able to cover large areas (up to 400ha, corresponding to 570 soccer fields) in a single fully autonomous flight. Depending on the flying altitude, it can achieve resolutions as small as 1cm. This combination and the ability to take off from anywhere regardless of terrain make Wingtra’s drones the instrument of choice for large-scale surveying.

name: Yuri Gravity
description: Founded in 2019, yuri enables research in microgravity for any industry. They develop fully automated micro-labs the size of a wallet and launch them in behalf of scientists around the world to the International Space Station (ISS), on orbital and suborbital spacecraft, on parabolic flights, and on drop towers. The unique environment of microgravity is especially valuable in the life sciences, as human tissue grows in three dimensions and drug discovery can be improved. The founders Maria, Christian, and Mark build on more than 30 years combined engineering experience in the space industry and have successfully brought 11 payloads to the ISS to date.

name: Zero Point Motion
description: Accelerometers and gyroscopes are everywhere – in cars, phones, robots, drones and in almost every electronic device that moves. However, mass-produced positioning sensors are reaching their performance limits. Zero Point Motion develops a chipset that allows highly precise navigation for the next wave of automation in vehicles and industrial applications. It is based on optical instead of capacitive measurement and is up to 10’000 times more precise than current mass-produced inertial sensors. The photonic technology enables military-grade positioning, indoors and outdoors, independent of GPS for industrial and consumer products that need affordable components.

name: Adam Valkin
description: I grew up in Johannesburg, South Africa, and made my way to the U.S. thanks to college tennis and curiosity. At Harvard, I studied Economics and History, and through a chance introduction, I landed my first job at an internet startup. That experience sparked a career full of adventure across tech, entrepreneurship, and investing – with chapters in London, New York, and Boston. I have spent two decades in venture capital, with the Hoegh family, Accel London, and General Catalyst. I’ve been fortunate to work with many exceptional founders and investors, and I’ve learned just as much from mentoring as I have from being mentored. I don’t take that for granted; it keeps me grounded and always learning. I’ve led early and growth-stage investments in Rapyd, Monzo, Melio Payments, Ro Health, Fiverr, Flywire, ClassPass, Superplay, GoCardless, Shift Technology, Finom, Spinny, Array, and others. I’ve also co-led or supported investments in Spotify, Lemonade, Blank Street, and Empathy. Along the way, I’ve incubated a few ventures too—including LOVEFiLM (acquired by Amazon), Propertyfinder (acquired by News Corp), and, most recently, Moment Holdings, a fast-growing payments company in Africa. These days, I split my time between Boston, New York, and Tel Aviv. I’m especially drawn to product-oriented founders who are passionate about shaping the future. I’m focused on early-stage AI apps that tackle familiar verticals, such as financial services, insurance, commerce, media, and healthcare.

name: Alex Moskowitz
description: I’ve never been good at separating the professional from the personal. For me, pursuit of professional excellence, becoming the best you can be at your craft, has always been a means for achieving personal growth. On a human level, I am a deep believer in the concept that you are a product of those you surround yourself with. It is then no surprise that I found in Vine Ventures the same ethos and values that I look for in personal friendships and life partners. Vine is a team who prefers to let our actions speak louder than our words. We care more about passing on opportunities in the right way than winning deals in the wrong way. We intend to keep our partnership small, knowing that we make our best decisions when we can be completely raw and vulnerable with our thoughts, and that requires complete trust. I’m the fourth investment hire the team has made in five years, and my path to Vine was non-linear. I grew up as the oldest of four siblings in Colorado, where technology entrepreneurship was an elusive concept to grasp. You have DISH Network, which famously never raised venture dollars, and then you have the likes of Vail Resorts, which I’m sure was considered some sort of startup at some point. There were of course others, but the point is, it wasn’t Silicon Valley. So I set out to learn: I moved to California to attend UC Berkeley and began gathering experiences that would help me understand how generational, enduring companies are built. I started my career as an investment banker with Moelis & Company and as a private equity investor with Lindsay Goldberg. Both firms had swanky offices in the middle of midtown Manhattan, and both experiences left me with a deep feeling of wanting something more inspiring out of life. The jobs were stimulating, don’t get me wrong, and I was objectively lucky to be there by all measures. But it wasn’t fulfilling on a personal level. I left to learn how you actually build companies instead of sitting in an ivory tower pretending to do so. I was fortunate to find great mentors in Marcela and Jess who were building Alfred, a software & tech-enabled residential management platform backed by NEA and Spark. It was a three year journey of the highest highs and lowest lows, one that gave me a deep appreciation for what it takes to build a generational company. After raising $150M in capital, launching new products, acquiring strategic assets, and helping to pivot the business to 4x growth in revenue, I decided to help many more founders through that same journey as a VC. I was fortunate to find OpenView as my first home in venture, a firm notorious for rigor in underwriting and creativity in firm building. OpenView had spent 18 years pushing the boundaries for how traditional venture firms service founders, and I take those learnings with me to Vine. When not working, I find joy in supporting my new wife and my three siblings on their personal and professional endeavors. You can find us chatting about the latest SciFi books/TV shows while snowboarding, at a concert, or at home with an ever growing list of feline/canine friends.

name: Barak Kaufman
description: I started my career cold-calling founders, “selling money”, on the investment team at Insight Partners with Eric Reiner. I subsequently left to start my own company, Intello (“SaaS to manage SaaS”). I made a ton of mistakes yet listened enough to find the need customers had with SaaS security, culminating in a successful exit to SailPoint in 2021. After the acquisition, I took some time to recharge while vesting & resting at SailPoint, incubating two health tech businesses on the side and running a few founder communities, including one for post-exit founders. I’m also an active angel investor. Most of my time is spent helping founders at the pre-idea and idea stage. Specifically, with post-exit founders who are navigating the “what’s next” questions. I love the 0 to 1 stage and plan to partner with epic founders building missionary companies for the rest of my career.

name: Dan Povitsky
description: Vine Ventures is the closest it gets to partnering with a VC that understands the founder mentality. We did not inherit a portfolio, an office, or investors; rather, we built our firm from the ground-up to deliver a world-class experience to founders, employees, and limited partners. Today, we are one of the largest seed-focused firms in NYC with a differentiated footprint in Tel Aviv and San Francisco. With the goal of being the go-to funding source for early-stage entrepreneurs in our target markets, I’ve relocated to each as we set up our operations on the West Coast and in Israel. I happily go where our team needs me most and am involved across significant parts of our portfolio, supporting founders in strategy, hiring, fundraising, and most importantly: balancing listening and speaking, always with a solutions-oriented approach. I started my career at Credit Suisse (in 2013, when the TMT group took Alibaba public) and TA Associates (investing and running global M&A for a portfolio roll-up). With an entrepreneurial itch, in 2018, I was fortunate to find in Eric Reiner a partner I aligned with morally, ethically, and in our mutual pursuit of becoming the best at our craft. Through a single family office-backed fund, we invested early in a handful of companies that became standouts of their vintage: Carta, Hippo, Roman, Unqork, and Front. That track-record and the support of founders and mentors allowed us to go institutional and launch Vine. Today, we support a diverse portfolio of entrepreneurs as their lead investors; and I’m proud to say we have helped them achieve a range of personal and professional milestones, including one of the highest graduation rates (from Seed to Series A and B) in the industry. I’m a big believer in focusing on your power-skill, embracing what makes you different, and developing your unique advantage to win. Test-taking not being my strength, as a teenager I focused on cross country and track to improve my chances in college admissions. Hard work (and coaches’ belief) became my ticket to the University of Chicago where I was lucky to earn enduring friendships, a couple conference titles, and a degree in Economics. To this day, I get the most enjoyment from team accomplishments and am grateful to work with founders and LPs alongside one of the best early stage investing teams in venture. When not working, I devote time to family and close friends, with whom I hope to be more often hiking, skiing, and adventuring.

name: Demren Sinik
description: The first sentence of a VC bio is supposed to be inspiring. Thankfully, I prefer to focus on second impressions. I grew up in Los Angeles and received my undergraduate degree from Harvard, where I was determined to study subjects that had no application to the real world. I majored in theoretical math because I obsess over logic riddles and minored in English because I obsess over Vladimir Nabokov. Little did I know these passions would manifest in surprising ways as a VC – whether in reading research papers, writing yet another blog post, or connecting on a deeper level with founders. After graduating, I moved to New York City and spent over three years at Blackstone Private Equity. Focusing on technology and business services sectors, I was privileged to partner with companies like Ultimate Software, Kronos, Vivint, Cloverleaf, and Gates. Having exposure early in my career to mature, public technology businesses – as an investor, operator, and BOD observer – has made me a profoundly better (and more empathetic) early-stage investor. I joined Vine as the first hire and now lead our efforts on the West Coast and LatAm. I’m a generalist but tend to index towards industries utilizing cutting edge technologies such as machine learning, data, security, and developer tools. Second impressions matter most because venture investing isn’t about the sales pitch on day one. It’s about showing up on day two – fielding your late night calls, finding your next 10x engineer, introducing you to a pipeline of eager enterprise customers. That’s the kind of partner I aspire to be at Vine. Anyone can write a check, but not everyone can invest. Backing the next cohort of generational technology companies is busy work. But in my limited free time, you can find me at the nearest cinema or taking extremely high risk bets on my skis.

name: Eric Reiner
description: Vine Ventures is an inseparable part of who I am. It is the embodiment of what I hope to accomplish with the “work” part of my time on this incredible planet. It is a family of like-minded individuals, looking to make money for incredible individuals and institutions, by backing some of the most heroic, brave, and determined creators in the world. We started Vine in 2020, receiving our first Limited Partner commitments days before COVID-19 broke out. Vine is a resilient founding team just like the ones we back; dedicated to innovating and developing the best user experience for founders beginning their process of creation. Before forming the team and capital behind Vine, I was with Insight Venture Partners, where I spent my days relentlessly searching for founders of growth-stage companies, and made investments in several including Xamarin (acquired by MSFT) and 1stdibs (DIBS – NASDAQ). Following Insight, I joined my friend Liad Agmon at Dynamic Yield to help build out the US presence of the Israeli software company that would ultimately get acquired by McDonald’s for a reported $300m. Immediately before Vine, I co-founded a venture capital firm called Sinai Ventures, backed by a single family office of one of the founders of SAP, where I was fortunate to lead early investments in companies like Carta, Hippo, Ro, Unqork, FrontApp, Ramp, Dutchie, and others. Vine is the outcome of a career and dream to combine our team’s experience and track record to build a new generation of venture capital firms.
